even when my body was cut limb from limb without anger— who can now afflict me?
Having already transcended afflictions to achieve perfect enlightenment, you maintain a mind of equal compassion toward all sentient beings;
forever free from envy and foul anger, there is none before you who is like me.
I have now shattered all the powers of Māra and am able to repel immeasurable koṭis of Māras;
I shall certainly grant you liberation—why then do you enter the city in such terror?
All those in the ten directions and in this land, Who dwell within these Buddha-fields—
I universally invite them all, Along with the hosts of Bodhisattvas of great supernormal power;
May they fill the entire world, And may their merit and wisdom perfume the world.
"Abide together with them according to the Dharma-style of the Buddhas, and likewise uphold that which all Buddhas have approved.

At that time, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of asankhyeyas of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others—all the great assembly—simultaneously raised their voices in unison and proclaimed:
"Excellent!"
He further spoke these words:
"Homage to the World-Honored One who is rare, unprecedented, and possessed of such immeasurable diligence as you are!
Homage, homage to the Greatly Rare, Unprecedented, and World-Honored One possessed of such immeasurable diligence as you are!"

He comforts all devas, humans, and the various classes of sentient beings, causing them all to receive deliverance; he causes the hosts of Māras to retreat and the accumulated impurities of the afflictions of sentient beings to be dispersed and extinguished; he shatters the mountain of self-conceit and cuts down the tree of rebirth; he grinds the wheel of birth and death and removes the darkness of ignorance; he engenders faith in those of external paths and dries up the four flowing rivers; he kindles the torch of the True Dharma and reveals the path to Bodhi; he bestows upon sentient beings gentleness and patience, and causes them to sport in samādhi and delight in the bliss of meditative concentration; he universally causes them to awaken to the path of the Four Noble Truths. This Great Compassionate Guide extensively delivers sentient beings, leading all devas and humans out of the sea of birth and death and into the City of Fearlessness.

At that time, the devas, humans, asuras, and others each scattered various kinds of celestial, exquisite flowers, incense, ointments, powdered perfumes, variegated jewel flower-garlands, and ornaments over the Buddha.

In order to make offerings to the Buddha, they swept and adorned the streets and alleys, covering the roads entirely with celestial jewel-garments, celestial exquisite flowers, and celestial fine silks.

Furthermore, they rained down various lotuses—*māndārava*, *pāruṣaka*, *karkārava*, *mahākarkārava*, *utpala*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka*—which followed wherever the Buddha trod and were spread beneath his feet.
On both sides of that road, celestial trees were manifested, their branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits all adorned with the seven treasures.
Upon these trees of the seven treasures further appeared various exquisite jewels and celestial ornaments for adornment, such as heavenly robes, crowns, earrings, bracelets, and armlets.

Between these trees are celestial flower ponds, their four sides and perimeters adorned with the seven treasures. They contain clear, cool, and delicious water endowed with the eight virtues, filled to the brim with various precious lotus flowers and birds of wondrous song, appearing in a vibrant array of colors.

Because those hosts of devas were making offerings to the Buddha, they each held in the air seven-jeweled banners, streamers, and flowered canopies, adorned with various golden cords, lattices, and pearl necklaces.
Furthermore, there rained down flakes of gold, flakes of silver, and flakes of lapis lazuli, as well as scattered powders of all kinds of aloeswood, tagara, black sandalwood, and tamāla leaves.
Furthermore, they rained down various powdered incenses, such as gośīrṣa, uragasāra, and candana, which covered the entire road.

They also rained down golden cords interlaced with pearl necklaces, maṇi-jewel necklaces, and wish-fulfilling jewel (cintāmaṇi) necklaces, which were scattered profusely through the air, swirling with the wind.
All the roads within and without that city were adorned with various celestial ornaments, and even the Māra within the city and his retinue were likewise adorned with exquisite celestial ornaments.

At that time, out of compassion for all sentient beings, the World-Honored One entered the Śūraṅgama Samādhi. With his mind in right concentration, he walked slowly along the road while remaining in that state of meditative absorption. He then manifested various subtle and wondrous physical bodies, with majestic deportment, marks and signs of excellence, and rare radiance. Standing upright in the middle of the road within the city, he caused all sentient beings upon that path to behold the Buddha’s body:

those who worshipped Brahmā and were to attain liberation through a Brahmā-body, the World-Honored One immediately manifested a Brahmā-body to transform and deliver them; those who worshipped Śakra and were to attain liberation through a Śakra-body, he immediately manifested a Śakra-body to transform and deliver them.
To those who worship Nārāyaṇa and can attain liberation through the body of Nārāyaṇa, he manifests in the body of Nārāyaṇa to transform and deliver them;
to those who worship Maheśvara and can attain liberation through the body of Maheśvara, he manifests in the body of Maheśvara to transform and deliver them;

to those who worship the Four Heavenly Kings and can attain liberation through the bodies of the Four Heavenly Kings, he manifests in the bodies of the Four Heavenly Kings to transform and deliver them.
To those who serve the Wheel-Turning Sage-King, he manifests in the body of a Wheel-Turning King to liberate them;
to those who serve various minor kings, he manifests in the bodies of various minor kings to transform and deliver them;

to those who serve those of great supernatural power, those who serve śramaṇas, and those who serve boys, girls, women, and goddesses, he manifests in their respective forms to transform and deliver them.

Even those who serve lions, dragons, elephants, rabbits, asuras, or various other species—whatever beings might attain liberation through the physical appearance, deportment, and characteristics of such forms—the Tathāgata manifests all those very forms to transform and deliver them.

When the World-Honored One had thus manifested these various demonstrations, all those sentient beings traveling upon the paths, having seen this event, joined their palms together, prostrated with their heads to the ground in worship and praise, and circumambulated the Tathāgata, experiencing what they had never known before.

All those beings—whether they be yakṣas, nāgas, asuras, or even those who are devas in the form of rabbits—who see the Tathāgata, perceive him walking upon the road with the physical form, appearance, and deportment of a rabbit.
All those sentient beings who have business with the Buddha will see the Tathāgata walking upon the road with the majestic deportment of a Buddha.
Those sentient beings will all join their palms in praise and prostration, following after the Buddha in unison as they walk behind him.
At that time, the seer Himavatprabharasa, together with his retinue of five hundred people, was sent by Māra to the great city of Rājagṛha to go to where the Buddha was.

At that time, Prabhāsa remained within the city gate awaiting the Tathāgata; he beheld the Buddha’s physical marks like those of a rishi, his majestic demeanor and features radiantly adorned, and saw him surrounded and venerated by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of devas.
Having seen this, he further thought:

"Such a person is truly a great ṛṣi, possessed of great protective power, and worthy of receiving the highest offerings of gods and humans; moreover, seeing that all his limbs are adorned like those of a noble sage, between the two of us, who is the more exalted?"
"Whose wisdom is superior?
How may I come to know this now?
He further thought thus:
"I should ask him further: by what birth is he born? By what clan?
And what does he uphold?"
"With what aspirations and inclinations? By what practices?
The seer Prabhārasa, observing his own disciples, spoke these verses:
"Now I see one of great learning and vast merit, Who can uphold the Great Practice and is worthy of offerings;
The Muni who best knows the path of goodness, Fully endowed with great patience, wisdom, meaning, and Dharma."
With all of you maintaining a heart of earnest devotion, constantly making offerings through great skillful means,
I shall, regarding this merit, hear his excellent teaching and cross over to the other shore.
At that time, the entire assembly of Prabhāsa-rasa, including Mañjama and the others, all spoke with one voice, saying:
"Such a Great Master should act in this manner."
Then the seer Kālakāma, together with his retinue, went to where the World-Honored One was. Having arrived before the Buddha, he stood with palms joined and spoke these words:
"Who are you now?"
The World-Honored One replied, “I am a brāhmaṇa.
The seer spoke again:
“What is your clan?
The World-Honored One replied,
“My clan is Gautama.”
The seer spoke again:
"What is your aspiration?
The World-Honored One replied:
"The three gates of liberation.
The seer spoke again:
"What kind of practices should one perform?"
The World-Honored One replied,
“I practice the suchness of the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi).
The seer spoke again:
“How long has it been since you went forth?
The World-Honored One replied,
“As long as that ignorance has existed, so too has my present going forth.”
The seer spoke again:
"Great Seer, such as you are, the constellations manifest their signs; do you perhaps recite what they clearly indicate?
The World-Honored One replied:
“I do not forget or set aside that which is thus equal. What does it possess? What is its solidity? Such a characteristic is known by the wisdom of the world.
The Rishi spoke again:
“This was said in order to cause joy to arise in the hearts of those who possess wisdom.”
The World-Honored One asked:
"What is meant by the phrase 'the constellations'?
The seer replied:
"The twenty-eight lunar mansions revolve in accordance with the sun and moon, each measured by the horizontal span of eight fingers of that person.

Twelve of those eight-finger spans constitute the measurement of the body; one eight-finger span is used for the measurement of the crown of the head, and one eight-finger span is for the measurement of the soles of the feet. Thus, fourteen eight-finger spans should be known as the phrase concerning the measurement of the lunar mansions."

If one understands it thus, there is no other dharma; for each person, the location of their birthmark serves as the definitive mark. If this were not so, O Great Muni, please listen as I shall now speak the verses on the lunar mansions.

"One born under the Mūla constellation has a dark-red mole four finger-widths below the corner of the right side of the face, with hair upon it; such a person possesses fame, wisdom, and rank corresponding to their station, and their power is most flourishing—such are the marks of one born under the Mūla constellation."

"One born under the constellation Aśvinī has a birthmark on the body measuring four finger-widths; he is intelligent, upright, and sincere, always abiding by the Dharma. Endowed with wisdom, a sense of shame, and honor, he possesses full rank and emolument; at all times his mind is ever courageous and capable of crushing formidable enemies."
"Those born under the Ārdrā asterism have a black mole four finger-widths below the neck; they are courageous and robust by nature, and possess full rank and emolument.

Those born under the Punarvasu asterism have a birthmark one cubit and a half below the crown of the head on the left side of the neck; they are prone to anger and delusion by nature, yet possess rank and emolument."

"Pūrṇabasu—whose name in the language of Tang means 'born under the lunar mansion of the Well'—shall have a black mole beneath his left armpit; he will be fully endowed with wealth and grain, yet possess little wisdom."

"The Muni was born under the constellation Puṣya—translated into Chinese as Guǐsù (Ghost-Su)—and possesses the most supreme marks: the wheel-mark upon his palms is like the solar disc; his hair is exquisite, upright, and curls to the right; his entire being is well-proportioned and his upper body is perfectly full; he is able to destroy the afflictions and acts as the Great Teacher."

"Those born under the constellation Aślesā (translated into Chinese as Liù, the Willow Star) have black moles on their chests; they are fond of fighting, prone to violating the precepts, difficult to dwell with, and by nature excessively lustful. These seven upper constellations are the Eastern Mansions."

"Moga (in the language of Tang, 'constellation') refers to those born under a constellation; if they have small moles on their chest or back, these are virtuous men who can practice according to the Dharma and possess abundant wealth."

"First, regarding those born under the lunar mansion *Citra* (translated into Chinese as *Zhāngsù*): they will certainly have a blemish to the left or right of the navel; they are generally stingy and short-lived.

Second, regarding those born under the lunar mansion *Svāti* (translated into Chinese as *Yìsù*): if one observes a mole four finger-widths below the navel, their rank, emolument, and observance of the precepts will all be ruined."

"Those born under the constellation Āśādā (in Chinese, the *zhèn* mansion) will have a red mole at the lower part of their navel. By nature they are fond of committing theft; they are sycophantic and crooked, possessing little wisdom, yet they are clever but of meager merit."

“Regarding those born under Citrā—the Star of the Horns in the Chinese language—whether male or female, there shall be a mole upon the genitals; they are upright by nature yet possess much lust, and furthermore, they delight in song and dance.”

"Regarding those born under the constellation *Sarvathī*—which in the language of Tang is called *Kang* (亢)—if a yellow mole appears either at the tip of the male organ or beneath it, such a person is by nature excessively greedy, causes anger and distress among the masses, and lacks wisdom."

"Regarding those born under the lunar mansion Suśaka (in Chinese, the Di constellation): if one has a red mole anywhere within a span of eight finger-widths from below the hip, such a person will possess a full circle of kinsmen and many servants; they will hold the rank of a high minister or official, be intelligent and modest, courageous and decisive in counsel, capable of repelling enemies, and constantly enjoy peace and happiness. Upon the end of their life, they will be reborn in the heavens. These seven stars belong to the southern quarter."

"Ānula, in the language of Tang, refers to those born under the constellation Anurādhā. If there is a small wart within a span of eight finger-widths above the knee, such a person will maintain the precepts with integrity and be fully endowed with rank and emolument."

"Those born under the constellation Śatabhiṣaj (translated into Chinese as *xin*, 'Heart'), who have moles on the inner thighs, will be short-lived, impoverished, and prone to violating the precepts; they will lack compassion and be detested and envied by others."
"Those born under Mūla (translated into Chinese as Wei-xiu) will have a small blemish upon their thighs; they possess merit, yet their family line will quickly perish.

Those born under the first Āṣāḍhā (translated into Chinese as Ji-xiu) will have a mole on their kneecaps; by nature they love giving, can understand the Way of the Dharma, and after death will be reborn in heaven."

"Regarding those born under the second *aṣāḍhā*—in the language of Tang, the constellation Dou (*Dou-xù*)—there shall be a blue mole upon the upper part of the right shin. By nature they are fond of quarreling and contention; people do not rely upon them, nor do they believe or accept their words."

"Those born under Śravaṇā—the Chinese term for which is 'Ox'—will certainly have two moles on the upper part of their right shin; they will always abound in rank and emolument, possess bodies free from illness, be beloved by others, and after death be reborn in heaven."

Regarding those born under the lunar mansion *Dhaniṣṭhā* (translated into Chinese as "Nǚsù," or the Woman Mansion): they have moles upon their shins, are prone to anger but possess little greed, and although they have wisdom, they lack noble rank or emolument. The seven mansions above belong to the Western Quarter; originally, there were few *Śravaṇā* (Vū) mansions.

"Those born under the constellation Śatabhiṣaj (in Chinese, the 'Perilous' asterism) shall have black moles within sixteen finger-widths below the knees; they are by nature foolish and will die by drowning."

"First, regarding those born under the constellation Bhadrapadā (translated into Chinese as Shìsù): from eight finger-widths below the bent knee, there will necessarily be a mark on the upper part of the thigh; this causes others to feel anger and vexation toward them, and they will be foolish, impoverished, and prone to committing theft."

"Regarding the second Bhadra—those born under the lunar mansion *Pi-xu* (Aśvinī) in the language of Tang—there shall be a mole within the tiger’s mouth; they are fond of giving, uphold the precepts, possess strong power of mindfulness, are wise and compassionate, and by nature have no fear."
“Revatī—translated into Chinese as the lunar mansion of Kui (Quí)—those born under this star are humble by nature and sustain themselves through manual labor.

Aśvinī—translated into Chinese as the lunar mansion of Lóu (Lóu)—those born under this star shall have a blue mole between the big toes of their feet; they will be free from physical illness and affliction, and will always possess great strength.”

"One born under the constellation Baraṇī (translated into Chinese as Wei, the Stomach), will have a mole on the sole of the foot; their disposition is devoid of compassion and they take pleasure in acting as an executioner. Having violated the precepts and committed evil deeds, they enter hell after death. This is a northern star."

What has been described above is precisely what is called the "phrase of the constellations. By means of this, one may know a person's character, their wealth or poverty, and their likes and dislikes; if one knows this, they can lead sentient beings to the further shore.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the seer, saying:

"This is what is seen by foolish worldlings; it arises from depending on the mind and adhering to it, dwelling in the activity of discrimination. It is a false vision produced by the feverish illness of worldlings."

Just as those such as dogs, snakes, fish, and turtles, or whatever other various sentient beings there may be who are born under the influence of the Puṣya asterism, they do not possess a portion of happiness; yet you have attained supernormal powers, meditative concentration, and liberation, and I, moreover, am able to manifest all things for you.
"Why do you not now question me?
At that time, the seer Kāśyapa was filled with great joy; he scattered flowers over the Buddha and immediately praised and entreated him in verse:
"The seer with the marks of a human form— I behold your most supreme marks."
Not knowing his lineage—whether he be a deva or a human!
His voice, speech, and manner are like those of Mahābrahmā;
his conduct and physical appearance are like those of an ancient seer.
Never before have we heard or seen one so fully endowed with the marks of a Muni;
what does your teacher proclaim, and what is your clan?
At that time, the World-Honored One replied to the seer with a verse:
"Because you do not know this shore or the other shore, You establish signs and conceptual constructs;
Bound by all manner of suffering, You are not a vessel for liberation."
The six perfections are my clan; the six supernormal powers are my Brahminhood.
He taught those six bases of respect, and the six sense faculties are cultivated through discernment.
There are three dharmas and three liberations; one knows them with equanimity as being without self.
When the bodhicitta was generated, at that time I went forth into homelessness.
Since a self-characteristic cannot be found, I skillfully cultivated signlessness;
seeing no person and no life-span, I knew that there is no self and all is empty.
The three feelings and the three modes of conduct—discerning that these are empty through cultivation—I have crossed to the further shore of wisdom; this is the peerless teaching.
Unattached like space, the one who acts with the mind of enlightenment,
Endowed with the power of patience, one shall attain such wisdom as this:
not clinging to any phenomena, there is likewise no recipient of retribution.
Understanding and conforming to suchness in this way, enlightenment is not difficult to attain.
Not abiding in any phenomena, nor relying on this or that,
practicing with the discernment of the limit of reality— one shall thus attain the Tathāgata.
Being signless and beyond the mark of conceptualization, one is free from anything to be grasped.
All phenomena are not a composite; this is what one shall attain as a Tathāgata.
Abandon these signs, and abandon the delusions of your own mind.
Your awakening will be equal to space; in this way, you shall become a Buddha.

At that time, while the World-Honored One was speaking these verses, in the very interval of that moment, the seer Prabhāsa and his retinue immediately beheld the World-Honored One’s physical form and majestic demeanor restored to the state of a Buddha dwelling [in the world]. They further regained their mindfulness, and as they reflected upon the roots of goodness planted long ago, those past merits manifested before them.
At that time, the Rishi Rasmi attained the Bodhisattva samādhi called Ratnaketu.

Regarding all the samādhis attained by Bodhisattvas, this samādhi perceives them all as if from atop a high banner; it observes the sovereign sphere of all samādhis, being unattached and independent of others' views, such that no one can destroy it and no one can seize it.
The Rishi Kāśyapa immediately stood before the Buddha with palms joined, holding flowers in both hands, and praised the Buddha in verse:
“O You of boundless renown who speak the truth, The world’s virtuous refuge,
The Tathāgata’s eye of wisdom Shines upon all sentient beings.”
Surpassing all sentient beings, Ever diligent and compassionate;
I bow my head to the steadfast one, The Guide who has exhausted all attachments.
With the light of purple-golden hue, He touches sentient beings with refreshing coolness.
Awakening all sentient beings through the merit of Bodhi;
the Buddha turns the Great Dharma Wheel, able to shatter the mountains of affliction;
having brought his final practices to completion, he has now attained the wisdom of Bodhi.
The great physician among sentient beings, adorned with the marks of reality, declares, "I shall attain Buddhahood.
The guide among sentient beings cuts through and destroys the net of all cravings; having crossed over himself, he delivers others as well.
Before long, you shall receive the prophecy of Buddhahood, becoming the supreme among men.
You will cause sentient beings drifting in the torrent of suffering to cross over the ocean of existence,
establishing them in the secure place of nirvana upon the path free from outflows.
All Buddhas of the ten directions, whose merits are like the great ocean,
act as my witnesses as I dedicate this toward the bodhicitta.
All sentient beings suffer from the most extreme and evil afflictions.
Throughout the three periods of time, may my own body, speech, and mind,
as well as those of all sentient beings, attain the bliss of Buddhahood through the extinction of suffering.
May all beings be fully endowed with this and attain the eternal nirvana.
The illnesses of sentient beings are extinguished, and the waters of affliction dry up;
having attained wisdom and the equalization of the faculties, their intrinsic nature is eternally firm.
Sentient beings arrive at the place of slaughter and undergo the bonds of manifold sufferings.
By the light of my merit, may all beings everywhere be swiftly liberated.
May every realm of sentient beings attain virtues as vast as the ocean,
obtain immeasurable merit and wisdom, and be fully endowed with all forms of happiness.
Abandoning those various evil views, Quickly draw near to right view;
Recalling their former places of birth, Sentient beings attain the practice of the Dharma.
All having obtained the boat of the Dharma, They cross to the further shore of the ocean of existence.
Having already crossed to the other shore, He attains all the dharmas of a Buddha.
Abiding for immeasurable kalpas, He universally rains down the great rain of Dharma;
With the pure water of the Dharma-cloud, He thoroughly washes all sentient beings.
Whatever evil I have committed through my body, speech, and mind, I confess it all;
may the Buddha alone bear witness to this.
Having conceived a heart of reverence, I shall never again commit evil deeds.
The Buddha is inconceivable, And may always be seen manifest before me.
If there be any merit, I dedicate it toward Bodhi;
For the sake of all sentient beings, I shall endure every suffering.
I exhort all sentient beings to practice the supreme path of Bodhi,
to purify all buddha-fields and kalpas, and the ocean of wisdom of all beings.
Having attained the purification of the buddha-field, may I realize Bodhi in accordance with them.
Having obtained a pure assembly, with pure patience abiding in the various stages,
and having attained the five supernormal powers with certainty, may I receive the lion’s roar from the Teacher.
O Guide who reveals unattached wisdom, please grant me your prediction.
If you shall surely attain Buddhahood, as the Tamer of all dharmas,
may the flowers I scatter become a floral canopy in the air;
may the multitudes of devas, nāgas, humans, and others all come to bear witness.
"I prostrate at the Buddha's feet, causing the great earth to tremble.
At that time, the flowers scattered by the seer Prabhārasa remained suspended in mid-air near the Buddha’s crown, merging into a single canopy.

When the ṛṣi Kāśyapa saw this, his joy became even more intense and beyond measure; free from all further expectations, he felt the highest delight and great rapture, and immediately prostrated himself, touching both knees to the ground to pay homage at the feet of the World-Honored One.

When the Great Seer Prabhāsa bowed at the Buddha’s feet, at that very moment, the entire trichiliocosm shook in six ways without interruption. All the immeasurable, incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) sentient beings—hundreds of thousands of koṭis and nayutas of them—assembled there, were filled with both sorrow and joy, and gave rise to great wonder and amazement at such an unprecedented marvel.

At that time, the Tathāgata manifests various bodies according to what each sentient being ought to see; to those who should be taught through the form of an elephant, they immediately perceive the Tathāgata in the form of an elephant and give rise to a heart of love and joy.

Furthermore, he saw the flowers scattered by the Great Seer remaining suspended in the sky above, transformed into a floral canopy, and the great earth shaking; having witnessed this, his sense of wonder increased manifold beyond measure, and he approached the World-Honored One and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
To all sentient beings who should be taught by means of a Buddha-body, they see the Tathāgata as having the marks and signs of a Buddha-body and conceive a sense of rare wonder.
At that time, the World-Honored One immediately arose from meditative concentration, rising with serene composure from the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.

The immeasurable sentient beings who were taught by the World-Honored One all saw him without any further longing; they were all greatly delighted and gave rise to hearts of love and joy, each offering as they had obtained—flower garlands, robes, powdered incense, ointment incense, and various ornaments—scattering them as offerings.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses of prediction for the seer Prabhāsa-rasa:
"Arise quickly and listen to this prediction; The Teacher now speaks it for you.
The Great Seer shall attain Bodhi, Where the earth trembles and a single flower-canopy appears."
Abiding in the space above, through incomparable protection,
you have attained the status of the Honored One among two-legged beings; sovereign in benefiting the world,
the Buddha possesses boundless merit, its measure equal to empty space.
"Solid within the three realms, the lamp of Dharma illuminates the world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Prabhārasa came forward, paid his respects, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"What will be the characteristics of the buddha-field that I shall attain, and in what manner shall I turn the great wheel of Dharma in that field?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Prabhārasa, saying:

"In a future age, after immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas have passed, there will be a world in the northern direction named Vikasitagandhā, fully adorned with such characteristics as those of the Land of Peace and Bliss (Sukhāvatī) in the western quarter today."

O virtuous mahāsattva, in that buddhafield you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and you shall be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Vimalagandhaprabhāsaśrī.

The lifespan of that Buddha shall measure ten intermediate kalpas; he will be accompanied solely by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas present, as he exclusively teaches the unsurpassed, pure Mahāyāna.

At that time, when the great assembly heard that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, had bestowed this prediction upon the seer Prabhārasa, each person offered the articles of worship they held to honor the seer.

At that time, five hundred māṇavas and ninety-two nayutas of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of sentient beings resolved their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and attained the bodhisattva samādhi called "not forgetting the mind of enlightenment."
The Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra, Volume Four;
The Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra, Volume Five.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Paramārtha of India during the Tang Dynasty.
Chapter Five: The Chapter on Characteristics.
At that time, the ten billion māras of the trichiliocosm conceived this thought:

"Now that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, is entering the gate of the city of Rājagṛha, we should adorn the interior of this city gate and its surrounding area with the most supreme ornaments, just as the devas, nāgas, and yakṣas have adorned the area outside the city."

At that time, the World-Honored One, through his knowledge of others' minds, knew the thoughts in the hearts of ten billion Māras, who desired to adorn the Buddha’s abode with the most supreme physical marks through their supernormal powers.

At that time, by means of his supernormal powers, the World-Honored One caused a Tathāgata and the great assembly to appear at each of the twelve gates within the great city of Rājagṛha, so that they all entered the city gates together.

At that time, ten billion Māras, using their supernormal powers, adorned the city gates, the surrounding grounds, the city walls, and all the trees with various ornaments—the most excellent among the excellent—and with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) arrays of decorative implements; they further embellished both the earth and the sky with sublime and wondrous adornments.

At that time, ten billion Māras together with their retinues—some assuming the form of Brahmās, and others even assuming the forms of great ṛṣis—each took their place within the multi-storied pavilions, windows, gates, watchtowers, parapets, among the trees, upon the ground, and throughout the sky.

They made offerings by raining down all kinds of flowers, powdered incense, burning incense, gold dust, and silver dust; as well as mani-jewels, pearls, various ornaments, finely embroidered garments, and other decorative articles.

Furthermore, with various celestial musical instruments, drums, and hand-clapping, they offered praise and sang hymns of the Tathāgata’s immeasurable merits; all gathered together to make offerings to the World-Honored One with such a foremost, most excellent, and greatly marvelous array as had never before existed and had never before been heard.

At that time, the World-Honored One stood beneath the city gate and touched the threshold with his right toe. Instantly and without interval, the entire trichiliocosm shook everywhere; likewise, all the Śakras, Brahmās, Sūryas, Candras, Lokapālas, Maheśvaras, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and other lords, as well as the devas of the earth, the devas of the water, the devas of the great oceans, mountains, cities, and towns, along with the multitudes of men, women, boys, girls, celestial rishis, and others, down to the palaces of the Akaniṣṭha heaven—all sentient beings obtained a great savor and their complexions became radiant.

All those in the assembly, seeing the great earth tremble and being awakened by the radiance, stood surrounding the ground and the sky of the great city of Rājagṛha, even scattering flowers, incense, and black sandalwood powder as offerings to the Buddha.

At that time, by the power of his supernatural faculties, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Buddha caused those scattered flowers and even the powdered incense to pervade as many lands as there are motes of dust throughout the ten directions—in every single direction, including all buddha-fields, whether pure or impure, empty or non-empty—so that they were offered and presented to each of those Buddhas.
From those various Buddha-fields, these scattered flowers, along with the powdered incense, ornaments, and other offerings, all produced the sound of these verses:
"May you quickly awaken and observe the practice of heedfulness;
This is the supreme cause of Bodhi. The cycle of birth and death flows on most grievously."
I now deliver you; you should swiftly renounce worldly affairs.
Recalling your past vows, the time has arrived for their fulfillment;
each shall receive the prophecy of awakening from the Muni Indra.
For the benefit of the world, he now enters the city of Rājagṛha.
The Great Sage, supreme and free from sorrow, having already subdued ten billion Māras, turns the pure wheel of Dharma; you should rejoice greatly.
Thus benefiting the world, you have universally displayed deeds of heroic vigor to liberate the world from suffering.
Now, for the sake of attaining bodhi as Māriṣa, I bestow upon you all this prediction.
Go swiftly to that buddha-field, where you shall behold wondrous and sublime adornments;
having attained such things spontaneously, enter that City of No-Sorrow,
and through the gradual practice of the path to enlightenment, you shall certainly attain Buddhahood.

At that time, by the power of the Buddha, the great assemblies in each of all the Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, as numerous as motes of dust, all beheld this assembly in the Bamboo Grove and each of those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas contemplating within their respective samādhis.

At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in contemplation within the Bamboo Grove, as well as the śrāvakas and mahāśrāvakas, all saw the World-Honored One staying at the gate of the city of Rājagṛha, taming beings and awaiting them.

That great assembly followed behind the World-Honored One and stood there; having seen the various verses emerge from within the great ornaments, they all completely filled all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions—fields as numerous as all atoms, whether pure or impure, empty or non-empty.
When the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and those dwelling as śrāvakas in those various buddha-fields heard this sound, they thought to themselves:
"From where does this sound of the Dharma come, which pervades such pleasing sounds?"
How exquisite, how lovely, how delightful, how pleasing, how inspiring, and how great is this sound of praise for such magnificent merit?
When they saw the rain of flower-powder incense falling, showering immeasurable adornments throughout the ten directions— a rain of countless flowers, incenses, and fine powders—
at that time those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and great śrāvakas abandoned their respective activities and were all greatly moved with wonder and praise.

At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata entered a samādhi called "Adorned by the Array of the Buddhas. Having entered this samādhi, immediately and without interval, all the great assemblies in the entire Sahā world-system and in all Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms of the ten directions beheld such signs of magnificent adornment within this Buddha-field.

Just as in that world of the Tathāgata Samantadarśin in a future age, which is a pure and undefiled mass adorned with merits, there is not a single thing—such as city walls or the like—that exists, yet it is naturally adorned.

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all the Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions—worlds as numerous as the atoms within them—all beheld the Tathāgata Śākyamuni residing in the great city of Rājagṛha, his radiance blazing and his appearance most majestic and sublime.

When the great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the great śrāvakas dwelling in those various buddha-fields heard these verses, they each called to mind and gazed toward the four directions; by the power of the realm of all Buddhas, they saw this world as if it were before their eyes, and they beheld the various adornments of the devas.
At that time, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and great śrāvakas had this thought:

"We shall certainly go to that land to the place of adornment within the Great Assembly, and there we shall universally observe the meritorious adornments of that buddha-field. Having seen Śākyamuni Tathāgata, we shall practice making offerings, and in the presence of that Buddha, we shall receive the prediction of our attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, by the empowerment of the supernatural power of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and great śrāvakas from worlds as numerous as the atoms within all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, each departing from their own Buddha-field, vanished and appeared here in the Sahā world in a single kṣaṇa, lava, or muhūrta.

At that time, from each of the ten directions, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields all arrived at this Buddha-field, filling the earth and the void, and remained there.
Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, each by virtue of the various roots of goodness and diverse powers of their respective bodhisattva practices, prepared and offered worship to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Setting this matter aside, there may be bodhisattvas in this buddha-field who rain down various flowers that completely fill everything as an act of worship to honor the World-Honored One;

or some may rain down various pearls, and even gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, *śarkara*, *musāragalva*, ox-head sandalwood, dragon-firm sandalwood, and *tamāla* leaves—all ground into powder—to fill the void as an act of worship to honor the World-Honored One;
or some may rain down various ornaments, decorative implements, garments, and embroidered silks as an act of worship to honor the World-Honored One.
Some raised various banners, streamers, and flowered canopies as offerings to worship the World-Honored One;

some burned various incenses, some scattered various jeweled garlands, and some played various musical instruments; some manifested various songs and dances, while others rained down various fragrant waters upon this land to moisten it; and some held various precious vessels filled with diverse jewels before the World-Honored One, offering them in worship.
Some held various precious vessels filled with scented water, adorned with flowers, fruits, and leaves, and offered them before the World-Honored One.
Others held various precious trees and various celestial robes, adorned with flowers and fruits, raising their hands to present them as offerings before the World-Honored One.
Some manifested the body of Mahābrahmā and joined their palms before the Buddha, and so forth, as extensively described in the previous account.
Others manifested the form of a lion and performed such prostrations before the World-Honored One.

By the power of the Buddha’s spiritual authority and the sustaining power of their own roots of goodness, those sentient beings were able to look at one another without their visual faculties perceiving any forms.

Because the Buddha, the World-Honored One, had manifested such signs, as well as the various realms created by Māra, the Great Realm Devas, and the Tathāgata himself through the bases of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of psychic power, faculties, powers, factors of enlightenment, the path, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—manifesting these various transformations of a Buddha’s realm—he followed behind the World-Honored One and entered the great city of Rājagṛha, proceeding toward the lotus grove in the middle of the main street.
When the World-Honored One arrived, he rubbed the lotus petals with his right palm and pulled them toward him.
As the lotus was thus pulled and moved, all the palaces of Māra and the seats where Māras dwell throughout this Buddha-field trembled violently.
All the male and female attendants of that Māra, as well as his followers and those who dwell there, were filled with fear and alarm; they spoke to one another, saying:
"Without cause and without reason, this palace of ours trembles so violently. Could it be that we, the realm of the Māra King, shall lose our positions?"
"Let it not be that the law of the destruction and disappearance of the palaces and dwellings in which we reside should arise from this!
We must now certainly investigate this.
At that time, having seen this matter, those Māras formed this thought:
"This buddha-field was formerly characterized by the five corruptions; who now is able to make it thus subtly adorned, so exceedingly delightful?

At that time, those Māras, together with their retinues, no longer saw their own dwelling places within their respective realms; they saw only the Śākya Tathāgata, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, fully adorned, his brilliance blazing and his light shining forth most intensely.

Throughout this entire trichiliocosm and all buddha-fields, various signs and physical forms of sentient beings currently dwelling therein appear everywhere; yet, there is not a single sentient being who can be identified.
At that time, all those immeasurable sentient beings saw before the World-Honored One the preparations being made for the act of offering.
Then those Māras thought to themselves:
"We shall certainly go to where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is; having seen him, we shall prostrate and ask our questions."
“Where have we, the Māra kings together with all our retinues, gone today?
At that time, one hundred koṭis of Māras from this Buddha-world, along with their retinues, went to where the World-Honored One was; having arrived, they stood respectfully before the Buddha.
Then that Māra bowed toward the Buddha, joined his palms in reverence, and spoke these verses:
"With a pure mind, I take refuge in the World-Honored One;
Quickly release me so that I may depart, And from this day forth, I shall practice the Dharma."
At that time, the World-Honored One replied with a verse:
"I do not obstruct anyone, whether they come or go;
if you can know the Path, go wherever you wish."
At that time, the Māra King spoke again in verse:
"As I desired to depart, And longed for my own palace,
I now see five kinds of bonds— The bonds of Gautama."
At that time, the World-Honored One replied in verse:
"I have severed all conceptual constructions; I have liberated myself from the world.
Since I am liberated from bonds, I cause others to be free from affliction and harm."
At that time, the World-Honored One, with his Buddha-eye, surveyed all things—the land of this buddha-field and the sentient beings filling the void—and spoke in verse:
“You who have now come from all directions, listen!
Casting aside all doubts and hesitations, each of you should remain silent for a while.”
In this world, a Buddha is difficult to encounter; the Dharma and the Sangha are likewise difficult to find.
It is difficult to possess pure faith, and the practice of bodhi is even more difficult.
To hear the Dharma in the presence of the World-Honored One is exceedingly rare.
To be able to cultivate the various forms of patience is difficult even at this time;
to subdue the mind is difficult, as is the cultivation of the practice of emptiness,
which can sever all conceptual constructions and all the evils of the world.
The practice of awakening is difficult to attain;
as I have practiced it in the past, I shall now explain it for you.
Even by speaking of but a single portion of a flower, I shall cause the darkness of ignorance to perish and manifest the unsurpassed path.
Those who have attained awakening shall now sever the three stains;
listen to the Great Teacher’s excellent teaching, which crosses over the various floods to the other shore,
abandons all great thirst and craving, and establishes the three doors of liberation.
You have established the three protections and so forth, causing all afflictions of the three realms to be dispersed and extinguished without remainder.
You have come here both to make offerings to the Triple Gem and for the sake of the Dharma.
Through the protection of the three times, those whose minds were shrouded by the delusions of the three times shall all attain supreme severance; they shall attain liberation from the three realms,
the patience that extinguishes afflictions, and the four kinds of inversions.
Deluded ordinary beings discriminate that which has no intrinsic nature;
they are not vessels for patience. With their eyes and other senses attached to various forms, and their body, speech, and mind shrouded in obscurity, they lack the four dhyānas.
Though dwelling amidst birth and death,
he was able to cultivate meditative concentration; he has now attained liberation,
being free from the four inversions, and has liberated all sentient beings.
Masteryfully uprooting the four flows, Understanding the arising and ceasing of all things,
Those who are disciplined and supple Shall attain the further shore.
The Bodhisattva, endowed with the four practices And with fearlessness, [shall likewise cross over].
Right knowledge can sever all the bonds of existence for sentient beings;
by understanding the five aggregates, one becomes untainted and free from the snare of bondage.
No longer subject to repeated birth, one reaches the further shore of the ocean of existence.
Before all these Buddhas, quickly confess all evils;
when all evils are severed without remainder, you will reach that shore of fearlessness.
All the sufferings of birth and death are experienced by those who follow conditioned existence.
Arising repeatedly in various states of existence, one follows after evil friends;
one should distance oneself from evil friends, sever evil views,
recollect the suffering of birth and death, and cultivate the ultimate truth.
One should drink the unsurpassed water and cultivate emptiness;
the ultimate truth has no substance, being neither real nor possessing marks.
The six sense faculties are like space; herein there is no agent.
Such is the nature of conceptualization; it is merely the conceptualization of non-existent phenomena.
The six sensations and the six cravings have the six contacts as their root.
Just so with the entry into the six contacts, one must also understand them to be empty.
Observing that nothing exists at all, such is the intrinsic nature of phenomena:
neither arising nor ceasing; herein one sees no reality.
All phenomena are identical to the Dharma-nature; throughout the three times, not a single thing exists.
If one knows there is no burning affliction, this path is most unsurpassed.
Free from the thirteen marks of self and the conceptualization of "sentient beings," if one thus cultivates patience (*kṣānti*),
one attains liberation in both this world and the next.

At that time, the World-Honored One, through the power of unimpeded merit and being free from fear, relying upon the roots of goodness he had planted, was able to manifest a great, perfect sound that pervaded the ten directions, and spoke these verses.

At that time, throughout the ten directions—in immeasurable worlds of the five turbidities, whether empty or non-empty, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and beyond—all heard this perfect voice expounding the Dharma. Having heard this sound, in each and every one of those immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddha-fields, all sentient beings became entirely free from desire; they possessed only a heart of pure love and joy, never regressing from the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* they had previously attained, and some obtained various *samādhis*, *kṣāntis*, and *dhāraṇīs*.

In the presence of this Buddha, immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings, having heard these words, meanings, and letters, immediately attained the stage of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*); furthermore, immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings each attained liberation according to their respective capacities within the three vehicles of the Dharma.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Prabhārasa, by means of his own supernatural power, manifested a staircase made of the seven precious gems and spread flowers all over it to form a lotus throne. Desiring to cause the Tathāgata to ascend this seat, he turned toward the Buddha with reverence, bowed his body, joined his palms, and spoke these verses:
"The Buddha, the moon of all-knowledge, beholds the world’s aging, sickness, and death, And those submerged in the distress of affliction— The moving and the unmoving beings of the world."
For their sake, he constructs the bridge of the Dharma;
the Buddha beholds the entire realm, where immeasurable and infinite sentient beings all stand with palms joined in waiting.
He distributes the assembly for the Dharma-giving and manifests that which he has attained himself.
Destroying the afflictions of sentient beings, With incomparable wisdom of skillful means, they manifest here universally.
They rain down the great rain of Dharma; All Buddhas of the ten directions,
And other great sages of wisdom act as witnesses for the Buddha.
The Muni-Indra has subdued the Great Māra;
his own nature is empty and non-existent, for he knows all phenomena to be like space.
Recalling his former vows, he turns the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma;
now he shall deliver those beings dwelling within the four currents.
The Lion-King among men, the Buddha, now understands this Dharma.
Causing them to cross the ocean of the three realms of existence, the Buddha has preached the peerless Dharma;
he removes the stains of the sins of sentient beings. The World-Honored One, with his great wisdom, benefits all living beings and establishes them upon the path of the Sugata.
At that time, the World-Honored One ascended the lotus pedestal upon a *padma* seat atop the jeweled stairs he had manifested.
Once the Tathāgata was seated, he surveyed the entire assembly in the ten directions and addressed the Māra King, saying:
"You should now give rise to joy; it is through your causal conditions that this great assembly Dharma-gate has now been attained."

When this Dharma was spoken, immeasurable and innumerable sentient beings attained liberation in both this life and future lives; they were universally delivered from the four torrents of calamities in the womb, old age, sickness, and death, abiding in the path of auspiciousness, and furthermore, they were caused to attain wisdom equal to space.
“Māra! With you now as their leader in this place, may the roots of goodness of all sentient beings increase. Māra!”
"You may request me to preach the Dharma, so that I may teach this assembly for the sake of those beings who are arrogant, enabling them to cross over the various floods.
At that time, the Māra spoke these verses:
"If Gautama is without fault, And is free from anger and pride,"
Why do you startle and disturb me by now preaching this Great Dharma?
If such anger and pride exist, how can one attain liberation?
I do not yet understand; O Muni, explain this to me.
At that time, the World-Honored One replied to the Māra King in verse:
“I dwelt for ten months in the womb, Experiencing the same conditions as those among men.
Though you, O Māra, wish to harm me, I harbor no impurity or hatred at all.”
I have endured all evils through patience, leaving no trace of defilement or impurity behind;
now that I have been born, you stir up the great earth and rain down stones to harm me.
Causing my milk to dry up swiftly, what kind of immeasurable and unpleasant things did they not do?
While I was dwelling in meditative concentration, these women sent forth to harass me.
Obstructing others so they do not give alms, Inviting me to be a king,
causing me to revolve in birth and death;
Furthermore, making the night dark, With military forces surrounding the city.
All this is your doing. You further unleash great winds and rains, causing the earth to become a landscape of ravines and pits,
with sand and stones heaped high to fill the roads.
Manifesting terrifying and foul sounds, you blow piercingly cold winds upon those places of ascetic practice;
when they wish to cross a river, you further unleash violent torrents.
Now appearing as a fierce lion, you further desire to kill me.
When I wish to eat and drink, you mix poison into my food;
you rain down vajra-hail, and a shower of swords, arrows, and weapons.
"You wished to defile the dharma robes of the *kāṣāya* in their entirety;
yet while I sat upon the Vajrāsana to benefit all sentient beings,
you then dispatched those women to harass me."
You and your host of generals do not remember when you harmed me;
at that time, I harbored not even a speck of malice toward you or caused you any distress.
Now that I have realized the Unsurpassed Way, I have already subdued you.
Now you are truly shameless, yet again you utter such evil words.
In the past, by means of wicked stratagems, you distressed Mahākāśyapa and others;
the goodness of immeasurable sentient beings was entirely destroyed by you.
Since you lack compassion, you now wish to harm me;
while I entered the city to beg for food, you released a fierce, intoxicated elephant,
Devadatta hurled down a great stone, and for three months I subsisted on coarse barley.
The foul cries of Sundarī, the fire-pit, and the poisoned food—all these were wrought by you;
they are certainly grave and evil karmas.
When you formerly approached the Tree of Enlightenment, you brought with you your military host and your awesome power.
Though they brought immeasurable swords and arrows, intending to harm me, not even a single hair of mine was moved; why then do you remain here?
Like one smeared with the poison of intoxication, you have roused ten million māras.
"Nayutas of sentient beings come to fill this buddha-field.
Know me thus: I abide in a heart of loving-kindness and compassion, feeling pity for all."
Yet you have constantly created extreme evil obstacles for me.
These venerable Munis, the Indras and Bull-Kings among men, all clearly perceive and know me.
Now, in this degenerate age, I perform the work of a Buddha;
for the sake of sentient beings, I abide in a mind of liberation.
Even if you inflict all manner of evils upon me, I shall never abandon patience.
I have no sense of envy, nor do I harbor any impure faults;
it is for the sake of gathering you in that I am thus constantly diligent.
I desire to bring you to tranquility; you should now request that I speak.
The Dharma of the foremost nectar brings about the cessation of the three realms.
To eliminate your evil karma for you, quickly purify your mind and place your reliance upon me.
I wish to bring you liberation; since you have long harbored an evil mind, you should abandon your wrong views and cultivate pure faith in your heart.
You should now realize this: before long, you shall receive the prophecy of your enlightenment.

At that time, Māra’s hatred toward the Buddha increased manifold; yet as he wished to depart from there, he realized he was bound by five fetters. He attempted to let out a terrifying cry but was unable to do so. Relying on the power of his own wrath, he emitted a hot, poisonous vapor; this vapor was so fierce and intense that it sought to harm the Tathāgata.

At that time, by the power of his benevolence and compassion, the World-Honored One transformed this foul vapor into a canopy of sumana flowers, which pervaded all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions. To all Buddhas who were dwelling in long life and peace while manifesting the teaching of the Dharma, the sumana canopy remained suspended in mid-air, close above the crowns of their heads.
At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in that buddha-field each asked:
"From where has this flower canopy come?
By whose spiritual power has it been manifested?"
Then those Buddhas each answered the question posed by the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O sons of good family!
There is a world named Sahā, impure due to the five corruptions. Therein dwells a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
By the power of his original vows, having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he now preaches the Dharma.
This is for the purpose of destroying the power of the realms of all Māras;
and for the purpose of establishing the power, the fearlessnesses, and the Buddha-realm of all Buddhas.
In order that the lamp of the seed of the Three Jewels and the teachings of all Buddhas may endure for a long time;
in order that all roots of goodness may increase; and by means of the power of diligence and spiritual transformations, to subdue all enemies who are non-Buddhists;

to cause the extinction of all terrors, inauspiciousness, and contentious debates; evil dreams and evil omens; internal and external enemies; strife, bondage, litigation, and discord; droughts, floods, famine, untimely rains, cold, heat, wind, dampness, pestilential vapors, and infectious diseases; and all evil sounds.
Because they cause all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and so forth to dedicate [their merit];
because they cause all kṣatriyas to likewise dedicate [their merit];
and because they instruct all four castes in the meaning of the Dharma, kindling the torch of wisdom and showing them the true path.
It is for the sake of causing all householders, cities, towns, villages, and those who adjudicate legal matters, as well as kings, royal palaces, and marketplaces, to fully dedicate their merits;
for the sake of ensuring that all the movements of the stars by day and night, the half-months, months, seasons, and years, proceed correctly;
and for the sake of ensuring that all five grains, flowers, fruits, and medicinal herbs reach full maturity.
Because all fields of craftsmanship and livelihoods shall not be lost, ensuring that what has been accomplished is brought to fruition;
because all faults and afflictions of body, speech, and mind are completely extinguished;
and because skillful deliberation, mindfulness, wisdom, and dhāraṇī, as well as valor, fearlessness, physical form, and eloquence, all increase.
Because it upholds the four noble lineages through the unobstructed, luminous awakening to all phenomena;
because it illuminates the Mahāyāna, increases the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and provides protection by comforting those on the stage of non-retrogression with the adamantine mind;
and because it brings about the single flavor of the ten stages.
They have attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) because they receive the office of a Buddha and establish bodhi;

they turn the great wheel of Dharma according to the manner in which they guide and gather those to be converted, universally covering all sentient beings with great compassion, abiding in the *pāramitās* and the unsurpassed path, raining down the rain of Dharma to satisfy sentient beings with the flavor of the Dharma;
they fulfill all the tasks of the Buddhas because they are liberated from the realms of all four Māras.
Because of establishing the realm of nirvana without remainder,
there is a dhāraṇī-seal named "The Distinctive Record of Entering the Phrases of the Dharma-Equality that Crushes with the Diamond Mind and Elevates the Object," which he wishes to proclaim.
"All Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past—named the *Vajrapramardana-cittodgata-pratyaya-dharma-pada-dhāraṇī-mudrā-praveśa-vibhaṅga-uddeśa*—upheld it and mutually rejoiced in it;

and all the Buddhas currently dwelling in the ten directions, sustaining their lives in the world, likewise teach that *Vajrapramardana-cittodgata-pratyaya-dharma-pada-dhāraṇī-mudrā-praveśa-vibhaṅga-uddeśa*, presently teaching, upholding, and mutually rejoicing in it."

In future ages, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all other Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas—whoever those Buddhas may be who shall appear in the world—will also preach this Vajrapramardana-cittodgata-pratyaya-dharma-pada-dhāraṇī-mudrā-praveśa-vibhaṅga-vyākaraṇa, and they shall likewise preach its upholding and mutual rejoicing therein.
At that time, the bodhisattvas from all those buddha-fields each requested their respective Buddhas, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What dharma is this?"

In the past, I had not heard this *Vajrapramardana-cittaudārya-dharmasamatā-mantra-mudrā-praveśa-viśeṣa-vyākaraṇa*, which is able to produce such immeasurable benefits, is able to fulfill such inconceivable dharmic advantages, and is able to act as the unobstructed illumination of all phenomena, even unto nirvāṇa.

When the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, proclaimed this Vajra-Crushing Heart-Exalted Dharma-Equivalence Mantra-Seal Entry-Differentiation Record, all realms of Māra’s power were extinguished, even unto their parinirvāṇa in nirvana without remainder.

For the sake of immeasurable benefit and immeasurable peace and happiness for all sentient beings; out of a desire to have compassion for the entire world, for the purpose of benefiting and bringing peace and happiness to the immeasurable multitudes of devas, humans, and sentient beings.
Then those Buddhas spoke to that bodhisattva, saying: "Good son!
We shall also go with you to that Sahā world, to the dwelling place of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

All the World-Honored Ones currently existing throughout the ten directions, whose lives are sustained and nourished, as well as all those World-Honored Ones in other worlds, are surrounded before and behind by all the bodhisattvas, with the assembly of śrāvakas attending them on both sides.

Those World-Honored Ones shall also proceed to that great assembly of Śākyamuni Tathāgata; and together with all those Buddhas, Śākyamuni Tathāgata shall likewise preach this *Vajrapramardana-cittaudārya-dharmapada-dhāraṇī-mudrā-praveśa-vibhakti-vyākaraṇa*. They shall collectively uphold it, mutually rejoice in it, benefit sentient beings, and obstruct the performance of evil deeds, for the sake of fulfilling noble conduct and attaining supreme wisdom.
All the Buddhas have now gathered there, surrounded and attended on all sides by bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas; they are all now present before that Buddha.

If you wish to obtain this Vajra-Crushing Mind-High-Condition-Dharma-Equivalence-Sentence-Dhāraṇī-Seal-Entry-Differentiation-Record, you should go there to hear it; furthermore, if you wish to make offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in all Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of immeasurable and incalculable Ganges Rivers.

At this time, for those who wish to behold the realms of the Buddhas, the realms of the Bodhisattvas, the realms of the devas, and the realms of the Māras—adorned with the magnificent arrays of Buddha-fields—which they have never seen before; and for those who wish to behold the assembly of immeasurable Buddhas which they have never seen before, now is precisely the right time.
"Let us go together with you to that world, to the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni dwells, to the Great Assembly Dharma-assembly.
Then those Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas each addressed the Buddha, saying: "So be it, so be it."
"O Great Virtuous World-Honored One!
We shall go together with the Tathāgata to that Sahā world to the Dharma assembly gathered by Śākyamuni Tathāgata.

At the presence of that Buddha, we shall listen for the first time to the *Dhāraṇī-seal of Entering the Distinctions of the Dharma-Phrase on the Mind’s Height, Destroyed by the Vajra*, for the sake of its specific records."

Because we have been able to make offerings to those immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, when they were gathered together at one time and dwelling in the world to nourish and sustain beings, and because we have heard their Dharma.
In this Sahā world, we have been able to behold those four kinds of miraculous powers and their adorned, universally embellished realms,
as well as the adornments of that great assembly of the Dharma.
"When we go to that buddha-field to recite this dhāraṇī, will we find a place to stay?
And will we be able to attend upon and make offerings to that Buddha and listen to the Dharma?"
"Furthermore, will those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have thus gathered as a retinue receive offerings?
At that time, each of those Buddhas addressed those great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and great śrāvakas, speaking these words:
"O sons of good family!"
"Do not doubt whether there is space for them to dwell in that world. Why is this?
Because the realm of all Buddhas enters into the skillful wisdom of boundless equality; it is the boundless ripening of sentient beings and the boundlessly vast expanse of space."
"O sons of good family!
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni is fully endowed with great skillful means.
O sons of good family!"
All sentient beings, those comprised within the realm of sentient beings, are merely the locus upon which the elements and sense-bases depend.

As for those sentient beings—if each and every one of them were to have a body as vast as Mount Sumeru—Śākyamuni Tathāgata is able to cause all those immeasurable sentient beings with such bodies to enter into a single mustard seed.

In the dwelling place of each and every sentient being, there is obtained a vast and spacious void; all sentient beings are so far apart that they cannot see one another. Thus, a body of such great magnitude enters a single mustard seed, yet no perception of increase or decrease occurs.
"Furthermore, son of good family!

All that constitutes the earth element which is solid and firm, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause it all to enter into a single most subtle *paramāṇu* (atom). Yet, those atoms of the great earth do not perceive any sign of increase or decrease. This is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom of skillful means, which he possesses in such fullness."
"Furthermore, good son!

All the moisture contained within the entire water-element, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause it all to enter into a single most minute hair-tip; yet that single hair-tip and the entire water-element do not perceive any sign of increase or decrease."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

All the warm characteristics of every fire-element can cause all fire-elements of the three periods of time to enter into a single most subtle atom (*paramāṇu*). Yet, those fire-elements, having entered into that subtle atom, function within their own domain just as they would in the vast expanse of empty space."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

All wind-elements that can be perceived, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause them all to enter a single pore. Within that single pore, all those winds move within their own domain as if they were in the vast expanse of space."
"Furthermore, noble son!

The Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause all sentient beings and their four great elements throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions to enter within a single most subtle atom (*paramāṇu*). While all those sentient beings and their four great elements perform the activities appropriate to their own respective domains, they do so as if in empty space without mutual interference; nor do they perceive any sign of increase or decrease in that single atom. This is called the Tathāgata’s wisdom of skillful means, which is thus fully perfected."
"Furthermore, son of good family!

Even unto all sentient beings comprised within the three periods of time, there are the six sense bases (*ṣaḍāyatana*), activities, grasping (*upādāna*), vows, sustenance, speech, sounds, letters, and the three modes of verbal expression; as well as the performance of karma, the differentiation of the aggregates (*skandha*) and elements (*dhātu*), and the various forms of cultivation and activity."

Regarding all those sentient beings, from the distant past, the arising and ceasing of birth and death within the six realms of existence encompassed by the three periods of time; even all sentient beings encompassed by the three periods of time who have passed through *kṣaṇas*, *lava-s*, and *muhūrta-s*; and even all sentient beings encompassed by the three periods of time, including the sensations of suffering and pleasure experienced and perceived by them throughout the three periods of time.

In a single moment, that Śākyamuni Tathāgata is able to fully awaken to and know all of them; he knows all their various characteristics in their entirety, yet the Tathāgata does not discriminate, being without discrimination or conceptual thought, knowing these characteristics as they truly are throughout the limits of the three periods of time.
“Good son! The Buddhas possess the skillful means of the wisdom that enters the sphere of reality, and they are fully endowed with the skillful means of impartially maturing sentient beings.

At that time, as the Buddhas were speaking of these characteristics of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, the various assemblies of those Tathāgatas in all directions—consisting of immeasurable and countless hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas—each attained the further shore of the sublime and wondrous spheres of their vows, wisdom, and supernormal powers.
The Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra, Scroll Five;
The Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra, Scroll Six.
Translated by the Tang Dynasty Indian Tripiṭaka Master Prajñāmitra.
Chapter Six: The Chapter on Dhāraṇīs, Part One.

At that time, in the eastern direction, there was a world named Abhirati, where the Buddha was named Akṣobhya. Together with immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and by virtue of the various protective empowerments and supernatural powers of the realm of all Buddhas, he set out from that place and, in a single kṣaṇa, arrived at this dwelling place of Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, within the four continents.
At that time, the Buddha Akṣobhya sat upon a lotus throne as he had manifested himself.

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas likewise, by the power of their own merit and supernormal faculties, manifested subtle and wondrous Dharma-thrones of lotuses, and sat upon the calyxes of those lotuses facing the Buddha.

In this way, from the foremost buddha-fields in the eastern direction—equal in number to immeasurable and incalculable atoms—various Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, who dwell there sustaining their lives, each Tathāgata, together with immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and assemblies of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of śrāvakas, set out from those lands in a single kṣaṇa and arrived at this place where Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, dwells within the four continents.

The great assembly that had come there, through their own supernormal powers, manifested subtle and wondrous Dharma-thrones in the form of lotuses; they sat upon the pericarps of these lotuses facing the Buddha.
At that time, in the southern direction, there was a Tathāgata named Ratnolkā (Jewel Star), and so forth, as extensively described, who sat upon the pericarp of a lotus facing the Buddha.
At that time, in the western direction, there was a Buddha named Amitābha; [the passage continues] with a detailed exposition, until [it says] he sat upon a lotus pedestal facing the Buddha.
In this manner, there is a Buddha in the northern direction named Dundubhisvara;
in the downward direction, there is a Buddha named Vairocana, and so forth, until reaching that lotus pedestal, where it is explained in detail as previously described.

In the direction above, there is a Tathāgata named Jñānaprabha, who, together with immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas—as numerous as the atoms in Buddha-fields as many as the sands of the Ganges—has come from that place in a single kṣaṇa, through the various empowerments of the Buddhas' realm, to this Buddha-field, to the dwelling place of Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, within the four continents.
When the Buddha Jñānaprabha arrived, he sat upon a lotus throne as he had manifested himself.

Once those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas had reached that place, each, according to the power of their own measured merit and supernormal faculties, miraculously created a subtle and wondrous Dharma-throne of lotus flowers; they then sat upon the calyxes of these lotuses facing the Buddha.

At that time, among the bodhisattvas who had gathered from the ten directions, some rained down Jāmbūnada gold as an act of worship to honor the World-Honored One, performing extensive offerings as previously described.

Some circumambulated all the Buddha-fields to the right; some, filled with longing and reverence, joined their palms before the Buddhas and listened according to the Dharma; and some dwelt in contemplation upon the portion of roots of goodness they themselves had constantly practiced.

At that time, the youth Subhūti, with palms joined in reverence, through his own supernatural powers and the protective empowerment of the Buddha’s spiritual power, caused the sound of the Dharma to pervade all buddha-fields, and spoke these verses:
“The Moon of the Muni, who has severed all doubts, has come everywhere.
Never before have we seen or heard of this; now all the assemblies appear in full perfection.”
All Buddhas are fulfilled, as are the Bodhisattvas of pure precepts;
all Buddha-fields are like shrines and temples, and all are worshipped with prostrations.
The Buddha has not come today without cause; the Sun of the Muni Buddha has arrived.
This land is defiled by the five turbidities, and its sentient beings are subject to corruption.
Now I shall subdue Māra and destroy the faction of darkness;
having gathered all wholesome practices, I have come for this very purpose.
Having heard the Dharma of tranquility, the hosts of Māra are utterly dispersed;
having given rise to a pure mind, you shall attain the state of a Samyaksambuddha.
Practicing the path of the Mahāyāna, you should don the armor of patience.
And in order to exhaust all afflictions, listen to this dhāraṇī;
each of you sit upon a lotus seat.
I shall now proclaim this method of protection, which encompasses and upholds all dharmas.
"The *Avinivartanīya-dhāraṇī* shall cause the True Dharma to abide for a long time,
and all obstacles shall be extinguished.
At that time, immeasurable and innumerable Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who had attained patience all spoke with one voice, saying these words:

“I only pray that the World-Honored One will sit upon the lotus throne; now, the Greatly Compassionate One, perfumed by supreme patience and great kindness, shall preach based on fearlessness to sustain all dharmas, eliminate the gates of all terrors, transcend the paths of Māra, topple the banners of Māra, establish the banner of Dharma, extinguish all afflictions, subdue all enemies, sever all doubts, enter all-knowledge, liberate from fear, serve as the supreme protection among all protections, and be able to reveal all dharmas to the bodhisattvas.”

That is to say: whether it be mindfulness, wisdom, the path, retention, non-forgetfulness, or skillful means; even including all practices for the accomplishment of peace and happiness, the basis for the merit of reliance and protection, samādhi, kṣānti, and dhāraṇī; entering into skillful and clear knowledge; and even maintaining the mind of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.

It is for the sake of causing the radiance and complexion of all sentient beings to be joyful; for the sake of power and renown; for the sake of delighting in dwelling alone; for the sake of increasing the eloquence of joyful speech, mindfulness, and retention; for the sake of hearing and maintaining [the teachings] without forgetting; for the sake of the retreat of all enemies; for the sake of the ripening of the five grains; for the sake of upholding the pure precepts; for the sake of perfecting the vessel of mindfulness; for the sake of the accomplishment of practice; and for the sake of reaching Bodhi.
“World-Honored One!

Now, for my sake, expound this dharani-method so that the True Dharma may be gathered and long endure, so that the lineage of the Triple Gem shall not be severed, so as to manifest the path to unsurpassed bodhi, because the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), suchness (tathatā), and space are without distinction; because all characteristics of light and darkness, and distinctions of ‘this’ and ‘that,’ are non-discriminative; because sentient beings, life-span, nourishment, and the concepts of self and person are without distinction; because all phenomena are equal in their mark of non-arising, non-origination, and non-extinction, being without substance, the limit of reality, and suchness without distinction; and because the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness are without distinction.”
“O Buddhas, World-Honored Ones!
