Now, as I proclaim this Dharma-door of the Mantra for Producing the Site of Enlightenment from the Nature of All Dharmas, immeasurable, innumerable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of sentient beings hear the Dharma; immeasurable sentient beings attain indestructible faith in the Triple Gem; all these sentient beings, acting as spiritual friends, mutually benefit one another; and immeasurable, innumerable sentient beings shall resolve their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, attain non-retrogression, and receive predictions of enlightenment, as they universally entreat all Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, to preach the Great Dharma.”

Those Buddhas, having silently accepted the invitation, immediately sat upright and composed upon the lotus pedestals and entered the samādhi of entering the realm of all Buddhas and the vow of equanimity.

Having entered this samādhi, he desired that all sentient beings gathered within all the Buddha-fields—every single one of them—should have all their sufferings completely extinguished, that all their roots of goodness should be brought to full perfection, and that they should attain the accomplishment of pure faith, mindfulness, and liberation.

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, perceive this very way: that within this buddha-field, all sentient beings who have come here—those with faults such as greed, hatred, delusion, views, pride, intoxication, arrogance, the view of a self, doubt, grasping, and the sinking of craving for existence—all their minds and mental factors are completely extinguished; every single sentient being understands it in this manner.
Yet, I alone stand before the Tathāgata with body upright to listen to the Dharma, not for the sake of others;

I alone am one whom the Tathāgata, with all his thoughts, observes in every aspect of my mind, whereby all my feverish afflictions are extinguished. There is no other person for whom the Tathāgata has been requested to speak the Dharma.

At that time, all the sentient beings within this buddha-field who had gathered for the assembly possessed sharp and keen faculties; with palms joined, they spoke with one voice to the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
"Teach us the Dharma,
O Great Virtuous One, Sugata!
Teach us the Dharma, so that we may together follow it and accomplish the Dharma of the Buddha, the World-Honored One."

At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, with a supreme and most wonderful fragrance that adorned him and surpassed all others, pervading all Buddha-fields, stood before all the other Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as well as within all the Buddha-fields, in order to make offerings to them.

The great assembly of all sentient beings who had gathered there further took up various jewels, various flowers, various garlands, various incenses, various parasols, various banners, various pennants, and various ornaments, holding them in their cupped hands and presenting them before the Buddhas as an offering.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata spoke these words:

"The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are single-mindedly mindful of me; all the World-Honored Ones currently residing in the various worlds throughout the ten directions have come from other worlds to question me."
In the past, my original vow was such: that I would attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within various defiled and evil worlds of the five turbidities.

These sentient beings have lost their refuge and lost the path of the Three Vehicles; they dwell in the dark chamber of ignorance, obscured by the shadows of afflictions, and are entangled on all sides by a mass of unwholesome dharmas. They abandon and distance themselves from wholesome dharmas, heading toward the three evil realms; they remain far removed from all who are wise and wise, acting as those who commit heinous crimes, those who slander the True Dharma, and those who revile the Noble Ones, relying instead upon those devoid of compassion. Out of pity for such beings, I shall exert the power of great compassion and the power of great diligence, and I shall endure all the sufferings of cold, heat, and exhaustion.
"I traverse cities, kingdoms, roads, and palaces on foot for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.
I partake of food that is meager, coarse, insipid, most loathsome, and unpleasant, for the sake of planting roots of goodness in all sentient beings."
He endures various coarse and harsh painful contacts, wearing garments of *śāṇa*, cotton, and coarse hemp; he takes up and wears such discarded rags as these.

I dwell in reliance upon mountain valleys, forests, thickets, empty houses, and among burial mounds; I accept even grass huts, coarse hemp, tree leaves, and all manner of harsh, foul-smelling, and unpleasant bedding. Through skillful means, I don the armor of great compassion and diligence.

"For the sake of all sentient beings, he teaches and demonstrates various things: for Kṣatriya kings, he teaches the dharma of sovereignty; for Brāhmaṇas, he teaches the four Vedas, astrology, and other such dharmas; for great ministers, he teaches the dharma of instructing and guiding sentient beings; for physicians, he teaches the dharma regarding the appropriate natures of various medicines; for merchants, he teaches the dharma of buying and selling; for farmers, he teaches the dharma of sowing fields; for women, he teaches the dharma of adornment, nurturing, and mastery over others' conduct; and for śramaṇas, he teaches patience, gentleness, meditative concentration, recitation of scriptures, and exhortation toward communal affairs."

Desiring to instruct and bring sentient beings to maturity—so that those who have not reached [the goal] may reach it, those who have not realized [the truth] may realize it, and those who have not been liberated may be liberated—they endure all manner of painful afflictions and roam among human beings for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of sentient beings.

"Even now, because of their jealousy, these sentient beings revile and slander me; they defame me with matters of lustful desire and further calumniate me with evil words, saying that I speak deceitfully, flatter, am crafty, hypocritical, false, and boastful, and that I engage in lewd talk with women."

Furthermore, they inflict harm upon me with evil deeds, raining down dust, filth, blades, poison, fire-wheels, iron hammers, arrows, spears, battle-axes, great stones, and other wicked weapons; they also bring against me mad elephants, venomous snakes, lions, tigers, wolves, water buffaloes, and fierce bulls, all together striking and hurling them at me with the strength of great warriors to do me injury.
"In my dwelling places and monasteries, they fill them with impurities, stench, and filth.
When my śrāvakas enter the city, these unrighteous beings, through unrighteous song and dance, incite the śrāvakas to engage in unrighteous acts."

By means of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of expedient means, they seek to harm me; it is because they wish to conceal the True Dharma, to extinguish the lamp of the Dharma, to shatter the ship of the Dharma, to disperse my assembly of disciples, and to topple the banner of my Dharma.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata spoke these words: “One should contemplate the Dharma protocols of the Buddhas of the past.

Just as those Buddhas, in this defiled and evil world of the five turbidities, convened a great universal assembly to establish sublime Dharma protocols—for the sake of causing the Sublime Dharma to abide for a long time, for the sake of shattering all realms of evil belonging to Māra, for the sake of ensuring that the lineage of the Three Jewels is not severed, for the sake of increasing the roots of goodness in all sentient beings, and for the sake of subduing all the discourses of externalists through the Dharma.”

It is for the sake of causing the extinction of all the miseries of sentient beings—famine, upheaval, strife, litigation, and pestilence; the imprisonment, verbal disputes, and threats from enemies of other regions; and the untimely cold, untimely heat, untimely winds, and untimely rains—as well as all faults of body, speech, and mind, and all evil views.

"In order to cause all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans to correctly dedicate [their merit], and to provide protection for all households, villages, cities, towns, and all places along the roads."
It is for the purpose of destroying all deceit, poison, sorcery, delusions, evil dreams, and signs of calamity;

for the purpose of providing nourishment through the flavors of all five grains, medicinal herbs, flowers, and fruits; for the purpose of instructing the Kṣatriyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras in virtuous conduct; for the purpose of causing the bodhicitta to flourish; for the purpose of diligently cultivating the various pāramitās; for the purpose of increasing the skillful means, wisdom, mindfulness, practice, valor, and eloquence of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas; and for the purpose of receiving the rank of Buddhahood, being comforted, and entering the further shore of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).

Just as those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past taught this Dharma-gate of the *Vajradharmasamādhi-hetupratyaya-cittavyavasthāna-saṃkṣobha-dhāraṇīmudrākṣarapraveśa-viśeṣavyākaraṇa*, they proclaimed it, upheld it, and mutually rejoiced in one another.
Excellent! Excellent! It is so, it is so.

"All the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, currently residing and sustaining their lives throughout the ten directions, have all come to this Sahā Buddha-field, this world of the five turbidities and evil age, to inquire after my well-being, each seated upon a lotus throne."

Because those Buddhas and others protect all sentient beings within this Buddha-field, they should proclaim this Dharma-gate of the Distinctive Record of Entering the Mantra-Seal Phrases for Establishing the Mind through the Causal Conditions of the Vajra-Dharma; they should expound it, uphold it, and mutually rejoice in it, so that the sublime Dharma may endure for a long time, so that the power of all Māras and evil realms may be extinguished—as extensively explained before—up until the attainment of the unobstructed wisdom that reaches the other shore, out of their compassionate acceptance and in response to my request, so that this Dharma-gate of the sublime Dharma may be established for a long duration within this Buddha-field, so that no heterodox paths can surpass it, so that the indestructible Dharma and the lineage of the Triple Gem shall not be severed, and so that all sentient beings may receive the flavor of the Dharma.
At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, spoke thus: "So it is, so it is.

We shall certainly perform such deeds for the sake of protecting and upholding this sublime Dharma so that it may long endure within this Buddha-field, for the sake of shattering the power of all Māras and evil realms, and even until the wisdom without obstruction reaches the further shore."

"We shall now proclaim this Great Dharma Door of the Great Dhāraṇī Seal, which establishes the mind through the causal conditions of this Vajradharma and differentiates the gateways of its syllables for shattering [obstructions]. You, the great assembly, should now listen with focused attention."
All the Buddhas assembled in this land and spoke this mantra:
"Tadyathā | aṅgala aṅgala | bhaṅgala ||"

I have never before heard this Dharma-gate of the differentiation of the Vajra-dhāraṇī-seal phrases—the method for establishing the mind through the causal conditions of the Vajra-dharma and so forth—which sustains the true Dharma of all teachers, ensures that the lineage of the Triple Gem is never severed, and is fully capable of shattering the power of Māra’s realm, cutting the bonds of Māra’s net, subduing the enemies of Māra, erecting the banner of Dharma, and protecting the divisions of the Dharma, even unto the fulfillment of the realms of all Buddhas."

Now, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, proclaim this Dharma-gate of the distinctions of the dhāraṇī-seal phrases; it is the great and rare practice of the mind-seal of all sentient beings, which subdues the six sense bases and leads all sentient beings to attain unsurpassed nirvāṇa.
When this method of the dhāraṇī-seal was being taught, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the sands of thirty Ganges Rivers accomplished this dhāraṇī and attained samādhi and patience (kṣānti).

At that time, the youth Candraprabha rose from his seat, joined his palms, and, through the power of the Buddha’s protection as well as his own supernormal powers, produced a great sound of the Dharma that completely filled this entire buddha-field, speaking these verses:
"The Buddha-moon is difficult to encounter, And to meet such an assembly is likewise rare;
An assembly of the wise is hard to find, As is one who practices the path of a bodhisattva."
Such a seal of the sublime Dharma is the foremost to hear.
The Tathāgata, the Greatly Compassionate One, is able to protect and uphold the True Dharma,
destroy all factions of Māra, and repel all enemies.
The Three Jewels shall never be severed, for all Buddhas uphold them;
All obstacles are destroyed and shattered, while patience and gentleness increase;
Through the dedication of sentient beings, the King and his realm are protected.
He restrains those who commit evil deeds and severs all wrong views;
he comforts all bodhisattvas and reveals the path to enlightenment;
he increases the pāramitās and brings the conduct of the noble and virtuous to fulfillment.
The wisdom of skillful means in eloquent exposition— increase such qualities as these;
uphold all the words of the Buddha, embrace all pure dharmas,
and protect the dhāraṇīs, thereby clarifying and purifying the path to bodhi.
Blazingly realizing the Dharma of reality,
one shall sever the net of doubt; having faith in the dhāraṇī is the path of fulfillment, namely, the attainment of bodhi.
We further wish to proclaim the dhāraṇī for protection, which guards those who preach the Dharma so as to increase their wisdom derived from hearing.
Who among you would grant their consent? This is the great renown of the Bodhisattva.
"And because one has attained freedom from hindrances, one is able to cause all sentient beings to increase in benefit.
At that time, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who were youthful, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, all spoke with one voice, saying these words:

"We now grant our empowerment for the upholding of this *dhāraṇī*. If there be any sons or daughters of good family—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—who shall bathe and purify themselves, don clean garments, adorn a canopy with various flowers, burn various incenses, provide various foods, and arrange various robes decorated with fine embroidery; who shall erect various exquisite banners, pennants, and flowered parasols to adorn the site of enlightenment (*maṇḍala*); and who, ascending a lion throne of soft and exquisite touch, shall expound and analyze this *dhāraṇī*—for them there shall be no mental distraction, nor disorder of the four elements, nor disorder of body or mind, nor shall any poisonous vapors come to touch their bodies."

There is no one who can cause him a headache; his internal and external limbs and four members are entirely free from illness or affliction, and there is no one who can cause his voice to become stammering or faltering.

"If that Dharma master has, in the past, any unwholesome karma such as disturbances of the four elements or disturbances of sound, by virtue of this dhāraṇī being recited by that Dharma master, all karmic obstructions will be extinguished without remainder, and he shall dwell in peace; furthermore, those who come to listen shall likewise have no disturbances of the four elements or disturbances of sound."
"If there be anyone who hears this dhāraṇī, all their unwholesome karma, the four great chronic diseases, and those with disordered voices shall be entirely extinguished.
At that time, the youth Candraprabha gazed up at the World-Honored Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of immeasurable Ganges Rivers, who were surrounded by a multitude of great bodhisattvas.
The youth Candraprabha bowed his body with palms joined and spoke these words:
"May the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, look upon me with compassion and grant me their consent; I shall now proclaim this dhāraṇī mantra."
Thereupon, before the Buddha, he spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
"Tadyathā | khaṇḍi | asamarūpe ||"

This dhāraṇī is exceedingly swift and possesses great power; it can ward off all enemies, fears, illnesses, and various calamities, and brings complete liberation from evil dreams and inauspicious signs. Because it is the basis for unobstructed wisdom, supreme wisdom, and the great accumulation of merit and knowledge, this dhāraṇī is taught.
At that time, the Great Brahma King, Lord of the World, by means of the majestic power and realm of a Great Brahma, transformed himself into a woman and sat before the Buddha Amitāyus.
He was foremost in physical beauty, with perfect features surpassing those of the gods; he was preeminent in being fully adorned with garments, flower garlands, and ointments used for decoration.
At that time, the Great Brahma King Lokendra rose from his seat, joined his palms in reverence, and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
You should protect my perfect voice as it expounds the Dharma, so that such sounds may pervade all Buddha-fields, enabling all to hear and know them without obstruction."
Just as I now [protect], these mantra-syllables shall skillfully protect and sustain both the Dharma-preachers who expound the teachings and those who listen to them.

Should there be, at a later time, Māras or the retinues of Māras; gods or male and female gods; or nāgas, nāga-girls, or the parents, sons, daughters, and retinues of nāgas; even piśāca-women, piśācas, their parents, sons, daughters, and their various retinues—whether human or non-human—who might seek out the faults of the Dharma-preacher and the listeners, acting as actual enemies while feigning the appearance of friends.

Regarding those who preach the Dharma and those who listen to it, even if they should suffer harm, injury, or contact that affects a single hair, or have their vital energy stolen, or be blown upon with poisonous breath, or be looked upon with an evil mind—even for the duration of a single thought-moment—I shall restrain and eliminate all such humans and non-humans, including the hosts of devas and māras. I shall cause them to become bewildered and confused, and I shall bind them by this solemn oath:

"I shall protect the perfect sounds with which the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, expound the Dharma, and I shall enable the sound of the Dharma to fill all Buddha-fields; I only pray that the World-Honored One will keep me in mind and assist me."
At that time, Amitāyus Buddha silently accepted the invitation.

Then, within the great assembly, there was a Śakra-devendra named Dhṛtarāṣṭra (Holding the Topknot), whose body was adorned with the supreme and wondrous radiance of a golden celestial crown; he sat before the Buddha, not far away.
At that time, the Śakradevendra Cūḍapanthaka addressed Īśvarī in this way: "Sister!
Do not sit before the seat of the Tathāgata Amitāyus with a defiled mind; do not disturb the World-Honored One."

Why is this? Delighting in conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) is the dharma of ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*); the Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, is forever free from conceptual proliferation. Conditioned phenomena manifest momentarily as the characteristics of arising and ceasing; all distinctions of names, forms, and phrases are suchness (*tathatā*). If you were to regard them otherwise, you would be misconstruing the Tathāgata.

Sisters! The Tathāgata is impartial, without opposition or contention; his single flavor is suchness, equal to the realm of empty space. Even empty space does not falsely establish itself; it is the mark of the exhaustion of the three types of activity. Just as empty space is without discrimination or non-discrimination, so too are all conditioned phenomena, and so too is the Tathāgata.

Regarding all the qualities of desire, one does not engage in conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), nor does one differentiate or fail to differentiate; rather, one abides nowhere, neither receiving nor grasping. Thus, there is no life-principle (*jīva*) and no being born (*jantu*); there is no nourisher, no person (*pudgala*), and no aggregates (*skandha*), elements (*dhātu*), or sense-bases (*āyatana*); there is no grasping and no conceptual proliferation.
"Sisters!
Why do you now engage in frivolous discourse before the Tathāgata?
At that time, the Tathāgata Amitāyus addressed the Lord of Devas, saying:
“You should examine the matter with careful discernment before speaking; do not utter words that are contrary to the Dharma, causing you to incur guilt and receive undesirable fruits.
This is a great virtuous man (mahāsattva), who has been taken under the care of immeasurable Buddhas and has planted roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas.”
Furthermore, this virtuous man, desiring to make offerings to the Tathāgata, has manifested the form of a woman adorned with exquisite ornaments; you must not say of him, "This is a woman."
At that time, the Śakra-deva Cūḍapanthaka addressed the Brahmā Lokendra, saying:
“O son of noble family!
Please arouse compassion and take me under your care; grant me joy and do not let me incur an evil retribution for these coarse words spoken now.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ānandadatta addressed the Buddha Amitāyus, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If this Śakra, Lord of Devas, does not repent these words, what karmic retribution will he receive?”
At that time, Amitāyus Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Prītimat, saying: "Good son!

If this Śakra, Lord of the Devas, does not repent his transgression, then throughout eighty-four thousand future births, he shall take the body of a grass-eating donkey and be held in contempt by others."
"Therefore, sons of good family!
You must always be cautious in your thoughts and guard this karmic activity of speech.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Brahma Lord Vaśavartin, saying:
“Good son! Speak as you wish; I have already protected what you have spoken.
Having received this protective mindfulness, Brahmā Lokendra rejoiced and, with palms joined, surveyed the ten directions and spoke these words:
“I only pray, World-Honored One,
that you will keep me in mind with single-minded attention.

If there are Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, or the assembly of Śrāvakas, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas who wish for the True Dharma to abide long in the world, may they all grant their consent to me here.”
If the Dharma master and the audience wish to attain accordance and harmony without disturbance or confusion, they should grant me their consent.

If those evil Māras, humans, non-humans, and others should cause disturbance to the Dharma-preacher and to sentient beings in future ages, I shall provide protection and, by making a solemn vow, sever their evil intentions.
When the sovereign Brahmā spoke these words, the sound that issued forth pervaded all Buddha-worlds.
At that time, all the Brahmā kings simultaneously raised their voices in unison and said:
"We, too, shall together grant our consent for this dhāraṇī."

Why is this? Because we, too, shall in the future uphold this dhāraṇī, and we shall protect those sons of good family in future ages who are able to reveal and expound such a Dharma-gate, as well as the assemblies that hear the Dharma; we shall cause them to attain accordance and correspondence with their aspirations.
"We now, before the Buddha-Bhagavān, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, and the great assembly of Śrāvakas, offer this *dhāraṇī*.
Then, that Brahmā Īśvara spoke these words:
"May the World-Honored One, together with the Bodhisattvas and the great assembly of Śrāvaka disciples, protect me."

Ghosts, Māras, and their retinues constantly come to seek out and watch for Kṣatriya kings and others who have received the consecration of office;
or they seek out and watch for queens, princes, princesses, and court ladies, even up to ministers, officials,
and other commoners who have attained pure faith in the Buddha-dharma— whether male or [female].
Whether they be women, boys, girls, laymen (*upāsaka*), or laywomen (*upāsikā*) who delight in hearing the Dharma;
or monks (*bhikṣu*) and nuns (*bhikṣuṇī*) who are diligent in meditation and recitation and remain heedful—
I shall provide protection for such as these against ghosts, Māras, humans, non-humans, and others who seek their vulnerabilities, even unto [the attainment of]...
He causes not even a single thought of malice to arise for the duration of a single kṣaṇa, let alone to cause them distress as much as a single hair.

"If there should arise those who, with evil intent, cause disturbance and destruction, seize their vital essence (*ojas*), or breathe poison upon their bodies—those who thus seek out and watch for their faults—by the majestic power of this *dhāraṇī*, the heads of such māra-followers, whether human or non-human, shall split into seven pieces; their eyes shall fall out, the water of their hearts shall dry up, and they shall suffer from white leprosy until their bodies rot with a foul stench. They shall lose their original supernatural powers and sink into the earth; further driven by malignant winds, they shall be cast into uninhabited places in the four directions. With dust covering their bodies, their minds deranged and confused, they shall flee in panic. Wherever they go, the ground shall crack open beneath them, and they shall fall into it to a depth of eighty-four thousand *yojanas*, where they shall die."

"If there are Māras or others who oppose this water-practice mantra, yet have attained pure faith in the Buddha’s holy teaching—such as bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs who diligently attend to monastic affairs—and if those spirits cause them distress and confusion, they too shall receive the evil retribution described above: their heads shall split into seven pieces and they shall lose their lives."

If this is the *Avinivartanīya-māramaṇḍala-dhāraṇī*, wherever it may be located, we shall diligently provide protection; for all sentient beings who delight in the Dharma, we shall protect them with a diligent mind day and night; and as for all those evil, venomous yakṣas, pūtanas, and the like, we shall drive them out from their domain.

"Wherever this dhāraṇī resides, I shall eliminate all strife, famine, foreign enemies, untimely winds, rains, cold, heat, and pestilence throughout all lands, leaving nothing remaining. Furthermore, I shall cause all the people of that country to achieve roots of goodness, so that they may live in accordance with one another, in harmony, peace, and abundance. I shall ensure that both the Dharma-preacher and those who listen to the Dharma attain far-reaching renown and remain free from illness and suffering; I shall also encourage the fourfold assembly of donors to provide them with offerings and sustenance."

At that time, within the assembly, there was a Great Brahmā King named Subhavyūha (Wondrous Sound), whose rank was that of a Mahāsattva in the tenth stage (*bhūmi*). He was the most honored among all the Brahmās among the Brahmās; the most honored among all the Māras among the Māras; the most honored among all the Śakras among the Śakras; and even among Vaiśravaṇa, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, the Asuras, and others, he was the most honored among all the lords of gods.

At that time, the Brahma King Wonderful Sound transformed himself into the form of a supreme woman, her physical features perfect and her deportment complete; adorned with the most excellent ornaments, she sat before the Tathāgata Śākyamuni with palms joined.

Holding a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) in both hands as an offering to the Buddha, he gazed upon the Honored One’s countenance with an unwavering gaze; his faculties were tranquil, and he did not perceive the Tathāgata through the marks of physical form.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Brahmā Ghoṣavatī:
"For what reason do you now gaze upon me without blinking your eyes, even to the point of observing me through the signless?"
“Good son! Is there even a single dharma that can be called ‘Buddha’?
Is there even a single thing that can serve as a name?”

Just as with the afflictions of greed, hatred, delusion, and ignorance—wherein there is the name-and-object condition for signs, signs condition ignorance, and ignorance conditions volitional formations, and so forth in detail; when signs cease, ignorance ceases, and the cessation of volitional formations is likewise.
The Brahmā Wonderful Sound said:
“It is truly as the Holy One has spoken. Why is this?
“Ignorance cannot be apprehended,
Blessed One!
If ignorance cannot be apprehended, from what do those twelve links of existence arise?”
"Could it arise from empty space?
Yet empty space itself cannot be apprehended.
The Buddha said:
"So it is, so it is.
Son of good family!
All phenomena are like space."
Why is this so? Space is devoid of substance and devoid of marks;

it is neither darkness nor light. It is without discrimination and free from conceptualization; it is without formation and without destruction, and is ineffable. It contains not a single thing and has no boundaries, yet it cuts through all things.
So it is, so it is. Son of good family!

The true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the Buddha-dharma is severed; the Buddha-dharma is suchness (*tathatā*); the Buddha-dharma does not grasp at this shore or the other shore; the Buddha-dharma neither decreases nor increases.

The Buddha-dharma is not comprised of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases; its essence has no boundaries. Whether as reality, substance, or characteristic, all such things are non-existent. The Buddha-dharma is without movement, without abiding, and is not established through false conceptualization; the Buddha-dharma is entirely beyond the path of verbal expression.
When this Dharma was being taught, eighty-four thousand sentient beings resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, an evil Māra spoke these words:

"If the Buddha-Dharma is like space—neither a thing nor expressible—by what wisdom or diligence, and through what arduous skillful means, do you trouble and disturb me, destroy my realm, and even seize the sentient beings within my realm? Furthermore, why do you teach sentient beings this illusionary art of neither coming nor going and being without substance?"
If you were to instruct sentient beings in this manner, those afflictions and their activities would no longer arise.

For what reason have you, for my sake, assembled in this Sahā world such immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, and great Śrāvakas; as well as Brahmā, Śakra, the World-Protectors, and Maheśvara, who possess great supernormal powers and great protective empowerment; and even the great assemblies of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, all coming together to fill all the Buddha-fields, so that this Great Brahmā, devoid of compassion, might speak such a mantra?
"Having heard this, we all suffer from headaches and experience great agony, even to the point that our bodies rot and emit a foul stench from head to foot.

At that time, there were also sixty-eight thousand Māra kings and their boundless, limitless hosts of Māras, including extremely wicked yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas, piśācas, and others, who all raised their voices in unison and cried out these words:
"As soon as our followers hear this incantation, our headaches intensify, our bodies all rot and smell foul, and we undergo the most grievous suffering."
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed that Māra, saying:

"Recall how in the past, when I sat at the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, your hosts of māras filled the eighty yojanas as well as the entirety of space, all intent on harming me; and even now, you have again come with an army of immeasurable koṭis to harm me."

I likewise shall thus summon immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and even humans and non-humans, so that they may all assemble; for the purpose of causing you and all other Māras, humans, and non-humans to be completely subdued;
to extinguish all suffering and attain the bliss of the great nirvāṇa of quiescence;
and also to instruct you in the nature of non-coming and non-going, which is devoid of intrinsic existence and like an illusory phenomenon.
Because all destinies, all cessations, and all arisings—the flow of craving for birth and death—are completely dried up;
and because it causes you and all sentient beings with wrong views to enter the realm of nirvana without remainder and attain parinirvāṇa.

"O Māra! You and your followers should now swiftly resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Then this headache of yours shall be liberated; by gradually practicing the Buddha-dharma of the emptiness of nature, it shall manifest before you, and you shall attain the realm of all Buddhas. Thus, surpassing the realm of Māras, you will obtain great benefit."
At that time, sixty-eight thousand māras, together with their retinues, cried out with one voice:
"World-Honored One!
We now resolve to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"How might we cause the Buddha-dharmas such as the emptiness of intrinsic nature to manifest before us, and even attain the rare benefits of the Buddha’s supreme and wondrous realm?
At that time, an evil Māra spoke these words:
"Even if it were to cause me a severe headache for the remainder of my final existence, I would never, by means of such deceitful illusions, give rise to the bodhicitta."
At that time, the Great Brahmā Wonderful Sound spoke these words:

"I, too, shall now before all Buddhas resolutely uphold this subtle and wondrous teaching of the Buddha-field, and disseminate the honored teachings of Śākyamuni Tathāgata within this world of five turbidities."

From this day forward, until after the parinirvāṇa of Śākyamuni, I shall cause this Dharma-transformation to remain ever-flourishing; and wherever there are lands with sentient beings of right faith, I shall cause them all to never regress and to swiftly escape the net of Māra.
If this Dharma-gate is not circulating in the world, I shall cause it to circulate.

Where it has already been practiced, I shall cause their faith to increase and expand even further. Toward all sons and daughters of good family in cities and villages, I shall provide protection and nurture with a compassionate heart, warding off what is unrighteous and instructing them in what is virtuous and meaningful.

Wherever this *Dhāraṇī-dharma-gate of the Non-retrogressive Māra-field* exists—even if only in written form—and wherever a Dharma Master ascends the lion throne, wishing to reveal and expound this dharma-gate, he should first recite these chapter-verses of the dhāraṇī with a sincere mind to summon me and my retinue. I shall personally go to that Dharma Master’s location to provide protection, causing the assembly listening to the Dharma to attain great auspiciousness.
Then, before the Buddha, he spoke this mantra:

"Tadyathā | Apame apame 1 | Ambale ambale 2 | Balim jane jane 3 | Puṣkare svāhā 4 | Śaluke 5 | Makaye 6 | Imi-mi 7 | Krimi-ri 8 | Kiticchara-mudali 9 | Mudara-muba 10 | Svāhā 11. "World-Honored One! [he said.]

Wherever a Dharma Master preaches the Dharma, one must first recite these mantra verses. With my pure divine ear, I shall hear their voices from the upper realms; if I do not go there to act as a protector, I would be deceiving all Buddhas of the past, future, and present, and may I never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Nevertheless, I am determined to go to where that Dharma teacher preaches the Dharma to bow at his feet and receive him upon my head; furthermore, I shall grant the Dharma teacher eloquence for joyful exposition, and cause all the suffering of illness, evil views, regret, and minds of false doubt belonging to both the Dharma teacher and the assembly listening to the Dharma to be completely extinguished.
“World-Honored One!
To whichever direction this Dharma-gate is taught, wherever there are those who can receive, uphold, and recite it, I and my retinue shall go to that place.”

May all strife, famine, illness, and distress; internal and external enemies; droughts, floods, and the disorder of cold and heat; and untimely winds and rains; as well as evil views and wicked deeds, be utterly extinguished.

The fears of humans, non-humans, and animals, as well as all inauspicious dreams, evil omens, wicked people, lack of moisture, bitter and unpleasant tastes, and foul odors and harsh textures—all such afflictions shall be completely eliminated.
Even lions, fierce beasts, venomous dragons, wild oxen, jackals, wolves, thieves, deceivers, humans, non-humans, and so forth—all such immeasurable fears are completely extinguished.

In order to enable sentient beings to obtain the requisites for happiness, I shall cause various grains, medicinal herbs, flowers, fruits, superior flavors, food and drink, clothing, houses, rugs, and bedding to be fully provided through the accomplishment of their karmic rewards. Furthermore, wherever this Dharma-gate circulates, I shall obstruct whatever is unbeneficial and ensure that all beneficial matters are brought to fulfillment.
If those sentient beings have faith and delight in the True Dharma and practice wholesome deeds, I shall instruct and guide them so that their merit may increase.

Now, before all these Buddhas, I establish this great vow: I pray that all Buddhas will compassionately regard me, causing the Buddha-works and great vows I perform to be fulfilled; through their fulfillment, may the bases upon which my intentions rely be satisfied; and through their satisfaction, may all that I, a man of purpose, undertakes be accomplished.
At that time, with Śākyamuni Tathāgata at their head, all the Buddhas, out of compassion and in order to embrace and sustain the Great Brahmā Wonderful Sound, spoke these words: "Good son!
"We shall bestow this dhāraṇī-mantra upon you for you to uphold.

Why is this? Should any Śakras, Brahmās, World-Protectors, the Four Great Kings, or other gods, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and so forth, give rise to impure thoughts toward the Buddha’s holy teaching, they shall all be subdued by the power of this mantra."
When the Great Brahmā Wonderful Sound established such deeds of a great man, the Buddhas of the ten directions simultaneously proclaimed these words:
"May the power of the Great Brahmā Wonderful Sound’s vows be fulfilled."
He then spoke the mantra:

"Tadyathā | cāmuṇḍe | cāṇḍālipiṣṭite | hāmre | hāmre | sarākṣe | varuṇasmi-khe | cāṇḍāpāha | carame | etacchau-pikha-amūla-piṣṭite | sarvabuddhadiśiṣṭe | svāhā. At that time, after the World-Honored One Śākyamuni had spoken this mantra, he said these words:
"O son of good family!"

This dhāraṇī can cause all Māras, Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors, as well as all other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras, to possess great radiance; it gathers in all humans and non-humans alike, causing them all to dedicate their merit toward the virtues of all Buddhas.
"If you are now able to receive and uphold such a dhāraṇī, you will indeed be performing the deeds of a great man.
The Great Brahmā Wonderful Sound said: "Bhagavān!"
"World-Honored One! By means of this female form, I shall now skillfully protect and sustain all women, and I shall skillfully bring all women to full maturity."

If there are women who loathe their female bodies and seek the marks of a man, they should receive, uphold, read, recite, copy, and make offerings to this sutra; I shall go to where those women are and fulfill their wishes.

If there are women who weary of the cycle of male and female existence, they too should receive, uphold, recite, copy, and make offerings to this mantra. By the power of such women upholding the mantra, even though they have not yet abandoned desire, they shall no longer undergo conception.

Furthermore, if there are women who are treated with contempt by others, bullied, or deprived of all pleasant experiences, they too should recite this dhāraṇī; through the majestic spiritual power of the dhāraṇī, all their aspirations will be fulfilled and all happiness will be accomplished.

At that time, for the sake of making offerings, for the sake of protecting and upholding this dharani-spiritual-power dharma-gate, and for the sake of fulfilling the vows of all sentient beings, Mahābrahmā took a mani-jewel in both hands and presented it as an offering to all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, all the Buddhas raised their voices in unison and said: "So it is, so it is,
O son of good family!"
"May you always be able to protect and uphold the Buddha’s teachings, fulfilling the aspirations of all sentient beings.

Chapter Seven: Embracing the Sublime Dharma In the *Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Chapter Seven: Embracing the Sublime Dharma, at that time there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Prajñāvatīrṇa (妙慧通達), who sat before the Tathāgata Jvalanaratna (勝珠炎). He was not far from the Tathāgata Śākyamuni. In the space of a muhūrta, he manifested the form of Brahmā; in the space of a kṣaṇa, he manifested the form of Māra; and even manifested the forms of Śakra and the gods of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin heaven.

Furthermore, he manifests in the forms of various lords of the gods, such as the forms of the gods of Nirmāṇarati, Tuṣita, and Yāma; the forms of the Great Sovereigns (Maheśvara) of the Four Heavenly Kings; or he manifests in the forms of yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, rākṣasas, pretas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and so forth.
They may manifest the forms of lions, elephants, horses, water buffaloes, and so forth, even displaying the various forms of animals.
In a single kṣaṇa, they may manifest birds, trees, mountain fruits, clothing, bedding, various medicines, and vessels adorned with jewels.

In a moment, he manifests the forms of bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs; in a single kṣaṇa, he manifests the form of a Buddha, or manifests eighty-four thousand various colors and marks, even including square and circular shapes and pure, wondrous appearances.
At that time, the Elder Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra rose, joined his palms, and addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, saying:
"World-Honored One!
By what cause and by what condition does this bodhisattva possess such eighty-four thousand pure and wondrous marks,
as well as bodies of various kinds, shapes, dimensions, colors, and species?
The Buddha told Pūrṇa:

"This bodhisattva possesses a sphere of the power of attraction through great merit that no śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas can equal. The bodhisattva-mahāsattva of wondrous wisdom and penetration, according to the sphere of the power of attraction in which he dwells, brings sentient beings to maturity; this is not the domain of any śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha. Following these sentient beings who fill the ten directions—whether in pure or impure buddha-fields—he constantly employs his unobstructed eye of wisdom to act according to their vows and intentions, for those entangled by such decay and affliction, and according to where they have taken refuge."

When this bodhisattva enters such a samādhi, they manifest with such physical forms and dignified deportment, complete with various colors and features according to the specific dimensions of each location, even to the extent of the form of a Buddha; in accordance with those beings to be transformed and delivered, they establish them all in the three vehicles and cause them to abide on the stage of non-retrogression.

If sentient beings, lacking self-mastery due to greed, engage in various kinds of craving and seeking, [the Bodhisattva] provides them with their necessities in order to sever that greed, and subsequently establishes them on the stage of non-retrogression.
If there are those who are ill and require medicine, he immediately provides them with it, and only thereafter establishes them on the stage of non-retrogression. Pūrṇa!

This Bodhisattva Wondrous Wisdom-Penetration can, within a single day, deliver as many sentient beings as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, liberating them from all sufferings and placing them on the stages of non-retrogression within the Three Vehicles.
Pūrṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
For how long has this son of good family been engaged in the work of a great man for the sake of maturing sentient beings?”

The Buddha said, “For as many eons as there are atoms in incalculable buddha-fields, this son of good family has set his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Having spent that much time receiving the empowerment of the power of samādhi and accomplishing the deeds of a great man, he has further passed sixty-four more incalculable eons.”
Pūrṇa said: "After how long from now will the Bodhisattva Prajñāśrī attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in which Buddha-field?"
The Buddha said:

"After another twenty-six hundred thousand great kalpas have passed, there will be a great kalpa named Able to Deliver (Nengdu), and a world named Maṇi-flower Filament (Manihuasu). The sentient beings in that land shall all have a lifespan of forty thousand years."

The Bodhisattva Sublime Wisdom shall attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi amidst those sentient beings who commit the five heinous crimes and engage in unwholesome dharmas; that Buddha’s name shall be the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha Unfolding Boundless Light.
For forty thousand years, the Buddha constantly performed buddha-activities, maturing sentient beings through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, even leading them to attain parinirvāṇa.
Thereafter, the Buddha Anantaprabha entered parinirvāṇa through the nirvana without remainder. Pūrṇa said,
“World-Honored One!...”
“Where will those sentient beings whom this bodhisattva previously brought to maturity be reborn?
The Buddha said,
“This bodhisattva previously made such a vow, not grasping for himself:”

"In each of the ten directions, may I behold all the Buddhas existing within as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an uninterrupted succession of worlds; if I do not behold those Buddhas, I shall not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

When I was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, I exhorted and inspired sentient beings, leading them for the first time to resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and I instructed, taught, and established them in the six *pāramitās*.
Those who have already reached maturity throughout the Buddha-fields of the ten directions, and those who have already attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may I also cause them to see me.

By the power of the adornment of such *samādhi* and through my protective empowerment, may I be able to perform such deeds of a Great Man within every single Buddha-field throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the atoms of dust. Furthermore, for those sentient beings in those various Buddha-fields who have committed the five heinous crimes and are incurable, and even those sentient beings fully possessed of unwholesome dharmas—may they, upon the end of their lives there, all be reborn in my land by virtue of the power of my vow.

"I shall become a bodhisattva, causing these sentient beings to plant various roots of goodness and establish them on the stage of non-retrogression; only thereafter shall my own body attain perfect enlightenment.
Such was the great vow of the Bodhisattva Wondrous Wisdom.
At that time, the Bodhisattvas who had come from all the Buddha-fields of the ten directions spoke these words in unison:

"We have now gathered here in this Buddha-field from every direction, and we are now able to behold the Great Teacher and the marks he possesses; we see this great assembly of Bodhisattvas endowed with great compassion, as well as the methods for establishing and destroying the Dharma-mind through the causal conditions of the Vajra-dharmas of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present—dhāraṇīs, seals, phrases, distinctions, gates, records, and ritual forms—which we have never heard before, and by which we may obtain hearing."
**Chapter Eight: The Chapter on Prophecy** At that time, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya addressed the entire assembly, saying:

"I exhort you, sons of good family—Brahmās, Śakras, the Four Great Kings, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all others who have attained pure faith in the Buddha's teaching and have come to this assembly—to behold all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as well as the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, Śakras, Brahmās, kings of the gods, humans, and non-humans, gathered here like clouds. Such a great sign as this is extremely rare to encounter."
"You who are now gathered here in this assembly should each make a vow before the Tathāgata.
In this buddha-field, whether in the present age or in future ages, you must be able to protect and uphold such a sublime Dharma, so that the lineage of the Triple Gem may always flourish."

At that time, there was a māra named Śāntapuṣpa, who took a vessel made of the seven precious gems and filled it with various flowers, fruits, and sprouts of all kinds of grains. He transformed his own form into that of a woman, endowed with exquisite beauty and supreme elegance; her physical appearance was so perfect that none could equal it, and she adorned her body with the finest garments.

Holding the precious vessel of flowers, he made offerings to the Buddha and spoke these words: “May all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, turn their single-minded attention toward me. Whether they reside in this world or other worlds, may all those Buddhas who have gathered here—may all such Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—now accept from me these flowers, fruits, and sprouts of all grains, filling this precious vessel as an offering.”
I only pray that you will, out of compassion, universally accept me and grant me the fulfillment of my vow for supreme enlightenment.

If, throughout this Bhadrakalpa, in all Buddha-fields, I were to give food, drink, flowers, and fruits to sentient beings in the form of a woman, and even bring them to maturity, may I, by the merit of these deeds, fully perfect the six pāramitās and attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; and may I provide for all the sentient beings I transform so that none shall lack anything whatsoever.
At that time, all the Buddhas spoke with one voice:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"Good son!
Since you are able to establish this great giving with a pure mind and make offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, I have already accepted what you have bestowed."

I shall cause you to obtain exactly what you seek and for which you have sought; even for as long as you seek, I will fulfill your wishes, so that you may achieve merit and achieve supernormal powers.
At that time, the Māra Śikhi-puṣpa spoke again, saying:

"In whatever cities, towns, or villages there may be those who are able to receive, uphold, and expound this sūtra, as well as those who transcribe its scrolls and make offerings to them—I shall cause all things in those kingdoms, cities, towns, and even in frontier regions where people dwell, such as groves, flowers, fruits, and the five grains, to flourish and reach full maturity."
"May all sentient beings in every place, even down to the birds and beasts that feed on flowers and fruits, be fully satisfied.
World-Honored One!

If there should be a single person in any region who, being destined to eat fruits, should die without having eaten them, I would now be deceiving all the Buddhas of the three periods of time and the assembly of noble ones here; furthermore, may I not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Except for those whose karma is exhausted or whose life-span has ended, may all flowers, fruits, and delicacies be universally available for sentient beings to enjoy.
By this cause, may I fulfill the perfection of generosity (dānapāramitā).

If there are sentient beings who eat fruits and seeds, may these beings give rise to compassion and benefit one another; by this cause, may I fulfill the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā).
If sentient beings enjoy flowers and fruits, may those beings give rise to a gentle and supple mind; by this cause, may I fulfill the pāramitā of kṣānti (patience).
If sentient beings enjoy flowers and fruits, may it cause them to strengthen their mind of diligent effort; by this cause, may I be fully endowed with the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā).
If sentient beings receive my flowers and fruits, and their minds and mental factors give rise to the perception of impermanence, by this cause, may I fulfill the dhyāna-pāramitā.

If there are any sentient beings, even down to birds and beasts, who eat flowers and fruits, may they all delight in the Dharma and abide in the emptiness of intrinsic nature; by this cause, may I be fully endowed with the Prajñāpāramitā.

"Furthermore, wherever this Dharma-gate is practiced, for all the various kinds of rice, wheat, beans, and diverse fruits belonging to those sentient beings, I shall apply myself with great diligence so that those beings may obtain abundant seeds and cause all their granaries and storehouses to be filled to overflowing."

If those sentient beings, even down to the birds and beasts that eat flowers and fruits, do so by this cause, may it cause me to be fully endowed with the *prajñāpāramitā*. He demonstrated four hundred and four kinds of root medicines, four hundred and four kinds of fruit medicines, four hundred and four kinds of medicines prepared by boiling with ghee, four hundred and four kinds of medicines prepared by boiling with oil, four hundred and four kinds of purgative medicines, and various *agada* (antidote) medicines for specific treatments, including decoctions, powders, and pills—medicines that collectively treat all ailments both internal and external throughout the body, totaling one thousand four hundred varieties.

For the sake of bringing all sentient beings to maturity, for the desire to eliminate the suffering of various illnesses, and also for the benefit of all sentient beings, I manifest all such medicinal herbs.

If we should attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, may the Buddha, the World-Honored One, accept us and exclaim, "Excellent!

If there should be any gods or humans who seek to destroy, disperse, or extinguish the sublime Dharma spoken by the Tathāgata, and if we do not diligently employ skillful means to obstruct them so that the sublime Dharma may endure for a long time, then we would be deceiving all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time; furthermore, may we never attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

"If there be any son of good family, or deva, or even human, who wishes to disturb or harass bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, and if we do not diligently employ skillful means to obstruct them so that their distress is extinguished, then we would be deceiving all the World-Honored Buddhas of the three periods of time, and we ourselves shall never attain Bodhi."

“If there be sons or daughters of good family who seek unsurpassed bodhi, and encounter dangers such as water or fire, poison, malevolent spells, or diseases such as fevers and chills that recur every day, every two days, three days, or four days; or if they face such terrors as those arising from devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kaṭapūtanas, kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, lions, dogs, and so forth; or various calamities and afflictions such as epidemics, hunger, and thirst—if there be such fears, by means of these dhāraṇī mantra syllables upheld by all Buddhas, ‘The Fulfillment of All Aspirations,’ may those who recite and contemplate them attain complete liberation, with the sole exception of the determinate karmic obstructions of previous lives.”
