Chapter Ten: The Chapter on Protection (*Rakṣāparivarta*). This is the first part of the tenth chapter of the *Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra*. At that time, in the assembly, there was a Buddha, a World-Honored One named Mandāravagandha, who addressed Śākyamuni Tathāgata, saying:

"When those past Buddhas came from various buddha-fields to this great assembly in this buddha-field of the five turbidities, they all together protected this Dharma-gate, and caused immeasurable koṭis of māras to naturally retreat and disperse."

Beholding all sentient beings with eyes of compassion, he causes those with evil views to be liberated; kindling the torch of wisdom, he establishes sentient beings upon the path of auspiciousness. When he expounded this Dharma-gate of the *Vajradharmasamayacittavyūhadhvajavidhvamsanadhāraṇīmudrāpadavibhaṅgavyākhyā*, he raised the banner of the Dharma so that all factions of evil might be utterly dispersed and driven away.

It is so, it is so! We, the Buddhas of the ten directions who currently abide in the world, likewise do so out of compassion and for the sake of nurturing all sentient beings. We have also gathered together in these defiled Buddha-fields of the five turbidities to protect this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate, even unto the establishment of the unsurpassed banner of the Dharma.

After the Buddha Śākyamuni, the Sun of the Dharma, has entered parinirvāṇa, who will be able to act as the foremost protector and upholder of the sublime Dharma in this realm, ensuring that the True Dharma blazes forth and spreads widely, causing all sentient beings to reach full maturity and enter the ranks of this Great Assembly?
"To whose hands shall we entrust this Dharma-gate?
Śākyamuni Tathāgata addressed Mandāravagandha Tathāgata, saying:

"All those who have long resided in this buddha-field—the Bodhisattvas who have attained forbearance, as well as the kings of the Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas—should diligently protect and uphold this wondrous Dharma-gate. Furthermore, regarding the sentient beings who have long resided within the four continents of this world and who have conceived pure faith in this Dharma-gate, the Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, and even the kings of the mahoragas, shall entrust this Dharma-gate of the pure dhāraṇī-seal into their hands."
At that time, the Tathāgata Maṇḍāragandha, with a voice of unobstructed perfection, pervaded this buddha-field and spoke these words:
"O sons of noble family!
Listen attentively!
Listen attentively!

It is rare for all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who come to this buddha-field to appear in the world; it is likewise exceedingly difficult for all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, to assemble in a single buddha-field within the span of a single kṣaṇa.

Thus, all these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have gathered here out of compassion for you; they have come to embrace and sustain all sentient beings, to protect and uphold the great Dharma-gates of all Buddhas, and to establish the unsurpassed path.

All Buddhas who enter the reckoning of the three periods of time today protect and uphold all earth elements, all water elements, all fire elements, all wind elements, and all space elements, so that this sublime Dharma may long abide in the world, so that the lineage of the Triple Gem may not be severed, so that all sentient beings may be brought to maturity, and even so that they may cross over to the far shore of birth and death.

At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as well as the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had long resided in those buddha-fields, the Śakras, Brahmās, and Lokapālas, the kings of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and other beings of great vital energy among the various classes of living beings, even down to all those dwelling within the world-systems of the four continents—all these assemblies spoke thus:
“O son of good family!
We entrust this True Dharma, protected by all the Buddhas, to you once more, so that all sentient beings may be brought to universal maturity.
You should always cause such an indestructible and non-perishing Dharma to blaze forth without cessation.

If there are sons and daughters of good family who possess faith, they should together uphold and transcribe this *Mahāsaṃnipāta* Dharma-gate. Furthermore, all those sons of good family—whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—who uphold, recite, and contemplate this Dharma-gate, you must constantly protect and provide for them, entrusting them with this Dharma-gate according to the Dharma.

If there is a Dharma master who delights in seeking the Dharma, delights in meditative concentration, delights in hearing the Dharma, and delights in upholding the Dharma, you should protect him and even provide for his needs.

Why is this? Because all those past Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who gathered in these defiled Buddha-fields of the five turbidities likewise entrusted the sublime Dharma to Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors, so that this sublime Dharma would not vanish, so that they might protect and uphold those who transmit the Dharma in the future, and even so that they might bring all sentient beings to maturity.

It is so, it is so. All the Buddhas of the ten directions who shall appear in the future, for the sake of gathering like clouds in a single kṣaṇa within the world of five turbidities to benefit sentient beings, shall preach dhāraṇīs, shall protect the sublime Dharma, shall entrust it to Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, and others, and shall provide all that is required; we, too, are now just like this.

“I entrust you further with all those who have long resided in this buddha-field, as well as the kings of the four continents—the Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas. Because they shall provide even greater protection and even greater support in future ages, you too should likewise keep this in mind and cause the indestructible Dharma, which is like a vajra, to blaze forth extensively.”

If there are sons or daughters of good family who, with faith, protect and uphold this Dharma; or monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who receive and uphold this Dharma; or even those who merely copy and maintain the sutra scrolls and place them within their homes; or those who are able to preach the Dharma and delight in listening to it; or those who diligently cultivate meditative concentration and uphold the Dharma—you all shall protect their wholesome intentions and provide for them with offerings and support.

Why is this? Because all Buddhas universally uphold this Dharma-gate. In whatever place—whether in a village, a city, a kingdom, a frontier region, within a royal palace, or in a forest hermitage—if this Dharma-gate is circulated, if it is revealed and proclaimed, if it is bestowed upon others, if it is recited from memory, or even if one merely copies the scripture and places it within one's home, by the power of this Dharma, these sentient beings will cause the essence of the earth and the vital energy of living beings to increase and flourish.

"By means of that vital essence and luster, may your diligence, valor, and strength all increase; may your retinues, as well as your fields and dwellings, likewise flourish and abound. May the king of men always receive protection, with his power and influence becoming sovereign, and may you also protect the realm within the king's transformation, constantly ensuring it is suffused with the flavor of that Dharma."

All the kings and rulers within Jambudvīpa should give rise to a mind of harmony and mutual benefit, constantly believe in karmic retribution, plant roots of goodness with a heart free from stinginess, always act for the benefit of all sentient beings, and always arouse a mind of compassion toward all sentient beings, even enabling the king to give rise to right view.

Each will naturally experience joy within their own land, causing those who practice virtue to fill the country; its abundance and happiness will double that of ordinary times, the essence and flavor of the soil will naturally become twice as superior, and there will be no flowers, fruits, medicinal herbs, or drugs that are not sweet and delicious. Grains, wealth, and treasures will also increase twofold, making every place delightful.

May all people be free from the suffering of illness; may all strife, foreign enemies, mosquitoes, gadflies, venomous snakes, evil spirits, rākṣasas, predatory birds, ferocious beasts, jackals, wolves, and lions, as well as untimely winds and rains—may all such calamities be completely extinguished.
Day and night, throughout the months and fortnights, as well as the seasons and years, all proceed correctly.
Most of these sentient beings practice the ten wholesome actions; when their lives there end, they are all reborn in the heavens and will again become your kinsmen.
Such immeasurable and abundant merits all arise from extolling this Dharma-gate of the Great Dharani of all Buddhas.

All these sentient beings shall cross over from this shore of birth and death to enter the realm of no-remainder; their fame shall increase and their karmic rewards shall be fulfilled. As for the female bodies they have planted, whether to be experienced in the present life or in future lives, by the power of this Dharma, all such forms will be completely exhausted.
The Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra, Scroll Eight;
The Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra, Scroll Nine.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Prajñāmitra of India during the Tang Dynasty.
The Remainder of the Chapter on Protection:

“Excluding only those who have committed the five heinous crimes, those who slander the True Dharma, and those who revile the worthy and the noble—the evil karma created by their body, speech, and mind, along with its retributive fruits, shall all be extinguished.”
If this Dharma gate, or even its written scrolls, are merely copied and kept within one's home, all their karmic afflictions—obstacles as vast as Mount Sumeru—will be entirely extinguished.

All roots of goodness shall increase; all portions of virtue shall be fully perfected; all that is hoped for by the mind shall be accomplished; and the virtues of body, speech, and mind shall all grow.
All evil views shall be eradicated without remainder, and all enemies shall be subdued through the Dharma.

One shall enter the path of subtle and complete quiescence, by virtue of the power of protection from this Great Assembly Dhāraṇī Dharma-gate, which is collectively upheld by all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.

"In whatever land this dharani-dharma gate circulates, it shall cause the richness, essence, and flavor of that land to be doubly accomplished; beautiful fruits and exquisite tastes shall increase, while bitter, acrid, and foul flavors shall be eliminated; flowers, fruits, wealth, grain, and all varieties of things shall be accomplished, and granaries, treasuries, and storage vessels shall all be filled to overflowing; clothing, food, drink, and medicinal decoctions used for sustenance shall be doubled and increased in excellence through the power of this dharma."

“If there are sentient beings who receive that food and drink, they shall attain freedom from illness and achieve a radiant complexion; their physical strength will be robust, their mindfulness firm, and they will joyfully seek wholesome dharmas while remaining far removed from all evils.”

When those sentient beings have passed away, they shall be reborn among your own kind; their retinues will increase, they will be endowed with full power that enemies cannot destroy, and by the power of the Dharma, they shall receive the protection of the four castes and be mutually instructed in the meaning of the Dharma.
"If you are able to act in this way, you will have already made offerings to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time.

At that time, the Tathāgata Maṇḍāragandha, in accordance with the sounds of wisdom and the meanings of the phrases suited to various capacities within the pure realm of all Buddhas, filled this entire world-system with the speech of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. He universally addressed all the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas within this Buddha-field, as well as the lords of the Śakras, the lords of the Brahmās, and the lords of the Mahoragas who dwell in this Buddha-field, further exhorting those who reside within these four continents:
"You should uphold and reveal this Great Assembly Dharma-gate of the words of all Buddhas, and protect the subtle and wondrous True Dharma of this sutra."
At that time, ninety-seven thousand koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had attained patience, led by Maitreya and all those dwelling in this buddha-field, spoke with one voice as follows:

"We now follow the instructions of all Buddhas; desiring to make offerings to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, we shall revere, uphold, and honor this subtle and wondrous Dharma-door of all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as we would the Buddha himself. Out of compassion to bring sentient beings to maturity and to establish them in the unsurpassed path," they said.

“In various villages, towns, cities, districts, kingdoms, royal palaces, and all places of tranquility, we shall widely disseminate and manifest this Dharma-gate in order to bring sentient beings to maturity and to ensure that this sublime Dharma endures for a long time.”
At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who had come to this land, spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!
You have performed what ought to be done."

At that time, all those dwelling in this land—the lords of the Śakras, Brahmās, and Mahoragas—along with the remaining assembly of sixty-four koṭis of nayutas of beings of great majesty and virtue from the intermediate states, all spoke with one voice, saying:

"We shall all receive, uphold, and even extensively reveal and expound this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate of the Great Assembly. For the sake of maturing sentient beings, for the sake of ensuring the long endurance of the sublime Dharma, we shall protect all who delight in the Dharma and listen to the Dharma."

"We now, in accordance with the teachings of all Buddhas, shall cause all strife, opposition, conspiracies, disputes, famine, chaos, hostile enemies from other regions, untimely winds and rains, untimely cold and heat, bitter and astringent flavors, as well as wicked people and evil things, to be entirely extinguished wherever this Dharma-gate circulates."

May there be peace, happiness, abundance, and harmony; may this sublime True Dharma be fully accomplished and cause it to endure for a long time. We shall redouble our diligent effort to protect and provide for the righteous kings of the land, as well as to protect all sentient beings who diligently cultivate meditative concentration.
At that time, all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, praised him with one voice, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
You all should now act in this way: by diligently performing deeds that benefit both yourselves and others, you will have thereby made offerings to all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Because you have diligently brought all sentient beings to maturity and caused this sublime Dharma to endure for a long time, you shall all swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, the Śakra and Brahmā lords of the four intermediate continents, up to and including the lords of the mahoragas, as well as those who were the foremost among those of great majesty and power, all rose from their seats, joined their palms in reverence, and spoke these words:

"We too, in order to honor the teachings of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, shall together illuminate and uphold this wondrous True Dharma for its preservation, and we shall duly receive this Dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī-seal protected by all the Buddhas of this Great Assembly."

"Furthermore, throughout all villages, towns, prefectures, counties, kingdoms, royal palaces, and places of tranquility, you should extensively proclaim and reveal [this teaching], and provide protection and support for those who uphold the sublime Dharma."

To all those who abide in faith and the true Dharma—Dharma masters and listeners, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and sons and daughters of good family—who believe in and accept this Dharma, or even those who merely transcribe the sūtra scrolls and keep them in their homes, diligently practicing meditative concentration: we shall protect and provide for them with various offerings, including clothing, food and drink, flower canopies, banners and pennants, ointments and powdered incense, and even all medicinal supplies and requisites; whatever they may require, we shall skillfully provide.

"If there are people who, regarding this sublime Dharma-gate, recite it, read it, or explain and proclaim it, we ourselves shall go to that place of the Dharma-seat for the sake of hearing the Dharma. Regarding them as we would the Great Teacher, we shall reverently honor and single-mindedly praise this Dharma-gate, and offer various canopies, banners, and streamers as offerings."

Why is this? When we extensively expound this dharma-gate of the dhāraṇī protected by all Buddhas, through the flavor of the Dharma, we shall obtain vital energy, be endowed with strength, endowed with diligence, endowed with resolve, endowed with mindfulness, endowed with wisdom, endowed with virtuous friends, endowed with a retinue, and endowed with all military forces, such that enemies cannot destroy us.

Therefore, we shall cause all strife, plotting, and litigation within every realm; famine, disease, and hostile invaders from other regions; untimely winds and rains, extreme cold and heat, calamitous droughts, and seasonal irregularities; evil dreams and ill omens; coarse, unpalatable, greasy, bitter, and acrid tastes; and all unwholesome factors such as wicked people and evil things—to be entirely extinguished. Furthermore, may there be double the peace, security, abundance, joy, health, and harmony, all of which shall be fully accomplished.

"The winds and rains shall come at their proper times; cold and heat shall occur according to the seasons; day and night, the divisions of fortnights and months, the seasons, and the years shall all proceed correctly. The constellations, planets, sun, and moon shall not lose their courses. Springs, ponds, marshes, and rivers shall all be filled to capacity. Wherever there are sentient beings dwelling, I shall block and sever any torrential floods that might cause them to be swept away or submerged."

"In those kingdoms, cities, towns, and villages, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, may all branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, roots, stalks, grains, and medicinal flavors become rich, glossy, radiant in appearance, delicious, and abundant. May wealth, grain, medicinal flavors, clothing, ornaments, and all such requisites be fully provided for all sentient beings, with nothing lacking."
"May those sentient beings who seek roots of goodness have their minds free from all evil karma, and may they fully accomplish a superior mass of merit as well as longevity.

For all villages and lands, I shall reveal this Dharani Dharma-door protected by all Buddhas; even if one merely writes it out in a scroll and places it within one's home, or reads, recites, and reverently makes offerings to it where the scripture is kept."

If there should be a Kṣatriya king who has been consecrated by coronation, I shall protect him and provide him with all that he requires so that he lacks for nothing; whatever is not beneficial, I shall eliminate for his sake, and whatever is beneficial, I shall grant to him accordingly.

All calamities, portents, agitations, and inauspiciousness; all evil views, evil deeds, and being possessed by evil; all evil vows, evil attachments, and deceitful flattery; all illusions, guile, false speech, jealousy, anger, and resentment; and all forms of stinginess—these shall all be extinguished. Right view, the right path, upright faith, self-mastery, single-mindedness, and a sense of shame and remorse—such dharmas as these shall all be taught and instructed.

"The consorts and queens, the ladies of the inner palace, the prime ministers and assisting officials, the treasurers, kinsmen, judicial officers, and generals, as well as all the people—including those of the four castes, men and women, and boys and girls—should likewise provide protection and support, and even offer instruction with a sense of shame."
In all directions, even including those with four legs, we shall likewise provide protection.

Wherever this Dharma-gate is proclaimed and revealed, or wherever the written scrolls or the dwelling places of these scrolls exist, we shall, through great diligence, protect all those sentient beings. We shall cause this sublime and true Dharma to shine forth everywhere so that it does not fall into obscurity; for this purpose, we shall exert the power of our diligence and perform such deeds.
At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, together praised those good sons, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! O good sons!"
"You should perform what is to be done in this manner; by means of this True Dharma and the seeds of the Triple Gem, you must exert yourselves so that they do not perish.
In doing so, just as you have acted, you shall have made offerings to all the Buddhas of the three periods of time."

Chapter Eleven: Protecting the True Dharma. From the *Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra*, Chapter Eleven: Protecting the True Dharma. At that time, the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, addressed the great assembly, as well as Śakra and Brahmā, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vaiśravaṇa, and the others:
“O sons of good family!

Out of great compassion for sentient beings, during this time when the Dharma is difficult to encounter in this defiled and evil Buddha-field of the five turbidities, I have made the vow to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Within this realm, sentient beings have fallen into the darkness of ignorance and are tormented by the treachery and malice of the enemies that are their afflictions. For the sake of extinguishing these afflictions for all beings, I shall repel the factions of Māra, raise the banner of the Dharma, liberate immeasurable sentient beings from all suffering, rain down the great rain of the Dharma, and defeat billions of Māras.
“O sons of good family!

Therefore, I now earnestly entrust this sublime Dharma into your hands. Just as these immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, and the countless and measureless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as well as the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who have gathered here from all places, [establish] through this Vajra-Dharma, the causal-condition Dharma-mind, the *Sarvadharmanirbhedadhāraṇīmudrāpadadvāra-nirdeśa-dharmaparyāya*, which protects the Buddha-fields and all sentient beings dwelling upon the earth.”

Because all faults and evils are extinguished, because sentient beings are brought to maturity, because all unwholesome karma is exhausted without remainder, because the lineage of the Three Jewels endures for a long time, and even until all Buddha-activities are accomplished—for these reasons, you should receive, uphold, and protect my sublime True Dharma, which can cause roots of goodness and meritorious practices to increase.

"If you recite and teach this to others, and if you establish others in the three refuges as upāsakas, cause them to dwell in pure brahmacarya, and cultivate various roots of goodness and meritorious deeds, these will increase;
if you cultivate the first dhyāna, meritorious deeds will increase, and so on up to the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling;

likewise, the roots of goodness and meritorious deeds pertaining to the fruit of srotāpanna, up to the fruit of Buddha-enlightenment, will all increase. These characteristics will cause the lamp of the sublime Dharma to shine forth in the present and into the future, enabling all meritorious deeds to flourish. For this reason, I entrust it into your hands."
Because the sublime Dharma realized by the Tathāgata must be made to blaze forth, I exhort you all so that your merit may increase; therefore, I entrust it into your hands.
If, in future ages, one even copies this Dharma-gate into a scroll and places it within their home, by the power of the Dharma, all evil karma shall be completely extinguished.

In whatever place one may be—whether in a village or a city—if one wishes to receive and uphold this [teaching], one should purify the body, don new and clean garments, scatter flowers, burn various incenses, spread various rugs and cushions, and adorn a lion throne; then one should reveal and expound this Dharma, preach this Dharma-gate, and even transcribe it into volumes to receive, uphold, read, and recite it.

If you do not go there to listen to the Dharma, but instead merely protect the Dharma teacher and those who listen to the Dharma, then because the evil karma of both yourselves and others will remain undestroyed, you will be deceiving all the Buddhas and will foolishly lose the true Path.
At that time, Brahmā Sahāmpati, the lord of the Sahā world, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Whether in the present time or in future ages, wherever this sublime and true Dharma may exist...”
Until it has been extinguished, whether in villages, towns, cities, districts, provinces, or kingdoms;
in remote border regions, royal capitals, or palace interiors; in monasteries (*saṃghārāma*), or places of solitude;
in the homes of brahmins, or the residences of great householders, or the dwellings of commoners; or among Dharma-preachers, bhikṣus, or...
The bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, and other faithful sons and daughters of good family,
delighting in bathing, anointing their bodies, and wearing fresh, clean garments, scattered flowers and arranged decorations to adorn the *maṇḍala*,
burned various incenses, spread various silks and brocades, prepared various flavors, and ascended the master’s [seat].
Sons of noble family, when you extensively reveal and expound this dhāraṇī-seal to others, whether writing it or reading it, I,
together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of my retinue, shall go to that place to surround them and listen to the Dharma.
For the sake of protecting those Dharma-preachers and so that the evil karma of both themselves and others who listen to the Dharma may be exhausted, I shall do so.
Because all wholesome dharmas are brought to maturity, because the great and wondrous True Dharma blazes forth,
and because one enters the foremost path of the light of great wisdom, I shall protect and defend those sentient beings in all those cities and even down to the households of commoners,
so that those sentient beings may have an abundance of wealth and grain and their storehouses may be filled to overflowing.
"If I do not come to hear what has not yet been heard, I shall have violated my former vow before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
At that time, the Brahmā King immediately spoke this mantra before the Buddha:

"Tadyathā | Aṅgūha-ceng-ga-pu-luo-tuo-na (1) | Yamitu (2) | Kha-kha (3) | Khava (4) | Khava (5) | Kīlinakhava (6) | Svāhā (7). When the Brahmā King had finished speaking this mantra, he addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If I do not come to listen to that Dharma-preacher, nor protect him—thereby causing his wealth and grain to abound, his storehouses to increase, and sentient beings to be fully satisfied—I would be violating my original vow.”

At that time, all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, along with the great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, and all devas, humans, non-humans, and others, raised their voices in unison to praise that Great Brahmā Heavenly King:
"Excellent!"
"Excellent!
At that time, Kauśika, the Lord of the Śakras, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

In whatever place, whether in the present or in future ages, even down to a village or city, if I do not go there to hear what I have not yet heard, I shall be one who has transgressed my former vow before all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
He then spoke this mantra before the Buddha:

"Tadyathā: kha-ba-mi-li-kha 1; kha-ba-mi-li-kha 2; na-kha-ga 3; a-mu-jo 4; a-mu-pa-ha 5; a-kha-ta 6; a-tu 7; ba-sha-tu 8; śī-na-ba-ra-ke 9; svāhā 10. When the Lord of the Śakras had spoken this mantra, he addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"If I do not act according to my former vow, it would be as if I myself were at fault for violating my own oath.
At that time, the great assembly, including humans and non-humans alike, all exclaimed in praise:
"Excellent!"
"Excellent,
Lord Śakra! At that time,
the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Bhagavān! In whatever place—whether in the present or in future ages—even down to a city or town—wherever this Dharma-gate exists, if I do not go there to provide protection, Bhagavān!”
"This is indeed a transgression on my part, as I have violated my own vow.
He then spoke this mantra before the Buddha:

"Tadyathā | okha (1) | navaṣada (2) | samudrācī (3) | dhātubhūta (4) | vāruna pavarāja (5) | svāhā (6). At that time, the great assembly, including humans and non-humans alike, all together praised Vairūḍhaka, the Great World-Protector, saying:
“Excellent! Excellent!
At that time, the Deva King Virūpākṣa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Whether in the present or in future ages, wherever this Dharma-door exists—even in a city or town—if I do not go there to provide protection and cause them to hear what they have not yet heard, I would be transgressing my former vow before the Buddha and thus become one who has committed an offense.”
He then spoke this mantra before the Buddha: "Tadyathā:
jaloge, ādage, ālemoge, ālemo, salendrava, pīyamojhe, svāhā. At that time, the great assembly, including humans and non-humans alike, all together praised the Deva King Virūpākṣa, saying:
"Excellent!"
"Excellent!
At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

Whether in the present or in future ages, wherever this Dharma-gate exists—even in a city—if I do not go there to provide protection for those who have heard what they have never heard before, I would be guilty of transgressing my former vow made in the presence of the Buddha.
He then spoke this mantra before the Buddha: "Tadyathā:

Piṇḍaśava 1, Khavaśava 2, Rāmukha 3, Kṣasara 4, Pūgavāha 5, Āmargavāṭa 6, Svāhā 7. At that time, the great assembly, including humans and non-humans alike, all together praised the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, saying:
"Excellent!"
“Excellent!
At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Whether in the present or in future ages, wherever this Dharma-gate exists—even down to a city or town—if I do not go there to provide protection for those who have heard what they have never heard before, I shall be at fault for violating my former vow in the presence of the Buddha.
He then spoke a mantra before the Buddha, saying:

“Tadyathā: 1. *cūḍāli*, 2. *cūḍā-cūḍāli*, 3. *khadāli*, 4. *ani-cūḍāli*, 5. *naya-nacūḍāli*, 6. *heṭi-cūḍāli*, 7. *sāgara-heṭi-cūḍāli*, 8. *saṃkucā-cūḍāli*, 9. *dharma-kṣaye-cūḍāli*, 10. *svāhā*. At that time, the great assembly, including humans and non-humans alike, all together praised the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa, saying:
“Excellent!”
“Excellent!

At that time, in this world, all the one hundred and twelve yakṣa generals and commanders who guard and protect these four continents, as well as forty thousand yakṣas who dwell within these four continents, and furthermore, the most supreme among those with great supernormal powers—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others—all spoke with one voice to the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Whether in the present or in future ages, wherever this Dharma-gate may exist—
until this wondrous lamp of the Dharma has ceased to burn— whether in a village, a town, a district, a county, a kingdom,
a royal city, a royal palace, a forest hermitage, or in the home of a brahmin;
In the houses of elders, householders, or commoners; or among Dharma masters, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās;
and furthermore, among all faithful sons and daughters of good family—one should bathe well, anoint the body with incense, put on new and clean garments, and scatter flowers.
He adorned and embellished the site of practice, spreading various carpets, mats, and garments;
he burned various incenses and filled pure vessels with various delicious foods, and prepared an exquisite lion Dharma-seat.

Once you have ascended this seat, as you extensively analyze, explain, and reveal this sutra for others, and while you are reading and reciting it, we shall each go there surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of retinues to hear the Dharma, in order to protect the Dharma teacher, and to protect our own assembly as well as other sentient beings.

"For the sake of protection and for the sake of maturing sentient beings, if we do not go to those cities and towns, even to the homes of commoners, and if we and our retinues do not accept their instructions or mature sentient beings, nor cause sentient beings to have an abundance of wealth and grain so that their storehouses are filled;

furthermore, if we do not eliminate all strife, famine, disease, enemies from other regions, untimely winds and rains, extreme cold and heat, and various calamities—then we would be deceiving the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present, violating our original vows and gaining nothing at all; we would contract leprosy, lose our supernormal powers, and our bodies would rot away."
“World-Honored One!

Although this is so, we, together with our retinues, whether in the present or in future ages, shall certainly cause the subtle and wondrous True Dharma of Śākyamuni Tathāgata to shine forth throughout the four continents of this world. Furthermore, we shall protect and provide for those who believe in this Dharma, fulfilling their needs so that their undertakings reach fulfillment and their evil karma is extinguished.”

We shall instruct and reveal this Dharma gate for those who preach it; furthermore, we shall cause both the preachers and the listeners of the Dharma to have abundant wealth and grain, so that all their requisites shall increase, and they shall fully uphold the indestructible and imperishable Dharma taught by the Buddha.

At that time, all those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, along with the entire assembly of humans, non-humans, and others, together raised their voices in unison to praise those devas, nāgas, and dharma-protecting spirits:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
"Excellent!
You have performed what is rightly to be done.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Ānandita addressed the Tathāgata Śākyamuni amidst the great assembly, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How is it that all these hundreds of koṭis of Māras, together with their retinues, have all come here?
The Buddha said:
“Good son! All these Māras, together with their retinues, have come to this assembly.
The Bodhisattva Huailè then addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"How is it, World-Honored One?
Do all these Māras, together with their retinues, attain pure faith within the Triple Gem?"
The Buddha said,
“No. Furthermore, son of good family!”
These one thousand followers of the evil Māras have found no satisfaction within the Three Jewels; lacking pure faith, they instead give rise to hatred.

Whether in the present or in future ages, until this sublime True Dharma has completely flourished, they will constantly and diligently employ skillful means to seek out its vulnerabilities, in order to cause the True Dharma to be destroyed and to vanish.
Furthermore, there were eighteen māras together with their retinues of thirteen thousand;
likewise, there were two hundred māras together with their retinues of two thousand one hundred.
All those māras found no satisfaction within the Three Jewels; lacking pure faith, they instead gave rise to resentment.

Whether in the present or in future ages, until this sublime and true Dharma has widely circulated, they will constantly and diligently employ skillful means to seek out its flaws, in order to cause my teaching and this sublime and true Dharma to perish and to vanish.

Why is this? Because from times of yore they have been sustained by the power of hatred and envy; because they have not planted roots of goodness; because they are possessed by evil associates; and because they have forever lacked hope and aspiration for the bliss of wholesome detachment and non-clinging.
"The minds of those Māras have never been in harmony with the mind of the Tathāgata or the mind of the Bodhisattvas, because they abide in impure faith and lack liberation.
Although these Māras do not now believe, they have beheld the sublime form of the Tathāgata’s great assembly and have heard this profound dhāraṇī."
"By these causes and conditions, at a later time, one shall attain pure faith and realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Bodhisattva Huailè spoke thus:
"How rare, World-Honored One!"
"How marvelous, O Sugata!

Even those sentient beings who have not planted roots of goodness, if they merely hear of or come into contact with this Dharma-gate, by such causes and conditions, they shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."

At that time, there was a Māra named Agati—who had previously made extensive offerings to the Buddha, possessed unwavering pure faith in the Triple Gem, and had received the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*—who arose from his seat in the form of a great ṛṣi. Joining his palms before the Tathāgata Śākyamuni and gazing upon the Tathāgata, through the empowerment of the World-Honored One’s majestic power, a great voice filled all buddha-fields as he spoke these words:

“May all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, keep me in their thoughts; and may all the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and Māra with his retinue, listen to what I say.”

Now this World-Honored One, Śākyamuni, the Greatly Compassionate Guide, made such a vow in the past: that in an extremely defiled and evil Buddha-field of the five turbidities, he would attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. For the sake of those beings who commit transgressions, who slander the sublime Dharma and revile the noble ones, whose mental continuums are fully possessed of unwholesome roots and associated with evil conduct—he universally causes them to transcend the three evil realms, brings them to maturity through the three vehicles, and enables them to cultivate patience, samādhi, and dhāraṇī. He leads them toward the pure Buddha-fields, ensures that the seeds of the Triple Gem endure without interruption, fulfills his great vows, eliminates all defiled Buddha-fields, and brings to perfection all adornments of merit.
"Therefore, we shall act in this way so that the True Teaching of the Tathāgata may long endure, and so that the sublime and correct Dharma may not perish or be destroyed.

Whether in the present or in future ages, no Māra or followers of Māra shall be able to destroy, corrupt, or cause the disappearance of the true Dharma received from the Tathāgata; they shall not even be able to afflict a single sentient being, with the sole exception of those few who follow [the path] in a compliant manner but lack complete faith."

If there are those who uphold this sublime Dharma, those who accord with this Dharma, those who preach this Dharma, and those who listen to this Dharma—whether they be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, as well as other faithful sons and daughters of good family—who diligently cultivate the three karmas and exert themselves, who practice seated meditation and recitation, who manage stūpas and monasteries, who constantly and diligently perform meritorious deeds, who diligently serve and make offerings to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and who diligently sever the fetters of afflictions within the triple world and diligently eliminate all the sufferings of sentient beings, causing them all to attain liberation.

If those practitioners are to be troubled by the emissaries of Māra, or by Māra daughters, Māra sons, or the retinues of Māra—who seek out their vulnerabilities to obstruct their wholesome deeds and create causes for a distracted mind—for their sake, I now invoke all the World-Honored Ones before me; may they grant me power so that my wholesome deeds may be accomplished, out of compassion for me.

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, together with all māras and their retinues, and all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—whatever beings have come to this buddha-field, as well as the multitude upon the great earth—out of a desire to benefit all sentient beings and so that the True Dharma of the Buddha may long endure, you should show me compassion and now grant me the accomplishment by bestowing this mantra.

“If Māra or his retinue should wish to afflict those persons and this Dharma, I shall subdue them, causing their minds to become disordered, their bodies to suffer pain, and their physical forms to shrink and retreat so that they lose their supernormal powers; for this reason, I speak these mantra-words.”

If any evil Māras, along with their retinues, male and female Māras, or Māra-messengers, should give rise to even a single thought of malice or impurity toward the Buddha’s teaching, or should disturb and trouble the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—even for a mere moment—desiring to cause such disturbance and cause them to fall away from their wholesome qualities; or wherever this Dharma-gate is revealed and analyzed, whether in villages, cities, towns, or even within royal palaces, or in remote border regions and quiet places—in whatever location it may be.
If one gives rise to a mind of destruction toward these [beings] for even a single moment,
then in those various directions there shall be strife, pestilence, death, famine, various diseases, hostile enemies from other lands,
untimely winds and rains, extreme cold and extreme heat, sudden floods, earthquakes, earth-roars, and falling meteors.
When such various evil signs arise, or when one intends to harbor thoughts of destruction toward flowers, leaves, fruits, grains, medicinal herbs, or flavors, at that very moment,
those māras and even their messengers shall be scorched by stifling heat,
defiled, putrid, and foul-smelling; they will be rendered incapable of action, unable to rise or move, and bound with the fivefold fetters.
He causes them to see for themselves that even all their limbs and joints become cramped and cannot be extended;

he causes them to fall into darkness where they cannot perceive light or color; he causes them to lose their supernormal powers and have their minds thrown into confusion, such that their six sense faculties can no longer engage with their respective objects.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying: "Tadyathā amale amale."

“Svāhā! Thirty. At that time, while the Non-Departing Māra was reciting this mantra, in a single kṣaṇa, because he had obtained the protection of the Omniscient One, all the realms of the Māras were utterly destroyed and nothing could be accomplished.
"It is so, it is so; all those who intend to bring about harm shall find that their aims do not bear fruit.
At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, together praised him, saying:
"Excellent!"
"Excellent!
All the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, and others likewise praised him together, saying:
"Excellent!"
"Excellent!
At that moment, the great earth shook violently, the four oceans surged and boiled, and all the kings of Mount Sumeru, along with Māra and his retinue, were utterly startled and agitated.

At that time, the malevolent spirits and others were likewise so, with the sole exception of those who possessed pure faith in the Buddha’s teachings and those bodhisattvas who had attained forbearance, who did not give rise to fear or terror.
At that time, the Māra King asked the Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati:
"Good son, by what causes and conditions does this Māra 'Non-retreating' possess such superior power?"
Who has acted against him?
This lack of compassion is the work of my followers and the power of my domain, by which everything has been scattered, extinguished, and utterly destroyed;
yet he has instead established the śramaṇa Gautama, along with his dark faction and kinsmen, to preach the nihilistic views of annihilationism.

As soon as I heard this dhāraṇī, my body became foul-smelling, putrid, and decayed, rendered incapable of any function; all directions became dark to me, and I could not see any light, being scorched by a great heat!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Dṛḍha replied to the Māra King, saying:

"This is due to the empowerment and protection of the spiritual power of all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and because all humans and non-humans have bestowed upon him this 'Power that Cannot Be Repelled. Therefore, all the powers within the realms of you Māras shall be utterly shattered, no matter what you attempt to do."
Now, as these words of the *Avinivartanīya-dhāraṇī* are being spoken, you should give rise to pure faith and, in the presence of the Tathāgata, resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"If you are now able to act in this way, you shall be completely liberated from all these painful contacts of body, speech, and mind.
At that time, Māra replied to the Bodhisattva Sthira:

"I would rather endure these sufferings now, allowing my body, speech, and mind to undergo immeasurable and incalculable matters of great pain and affliction until the very end of the kalpa; yet, I will never give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."

Chapter Twelve: Āṭavaka. At that time, among the host of yakṣas, there was a great general named Āṭavaka, who assumed the terrifying form of a yakṣa;
furthermore, there was a yakṣa named Saṃjñā, who assumed the form of a deer.
Furthermore, there was a yakṣa named Jñānolkā who had assumed the form of a monkey;
another yakṣa named Tṛṣṇāparityāga who had assumed the form of a billy goat;
and another yakṣa named Srotocchedaka who had assumed the form of an elephant.
These five yakṣas are virtuous beings who dwell not far from Śākyamuni Tathāgata, sitting before Kauṇḍinyaka Tathāgata.
From every part of their bodies, these five men emit pure, subtle, and wondrous fragrant light; each, with both hands, holds a great jewel of radiance as an offering to the World-Honored One.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Rativara, with a pure mind, perceived that those five persons were actually Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas based upon their pure reliance; he then addressed the great yakṣa general Aṭavaka, saying: "O noble son!
"What meaning do you now perceive that leads you to manifest such signs, deportment, and acts of worship toward the World-Honored One?
At that time, Aṭavaka replied to the Bodhisattva Abhirati:
"O son of good family!"
In the past, ninety-one kalpas ago, there was a Buddha who appeared in this buddha-field, named Vipaśyin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
During the time of that Buddha’s world, we brothers were born of the same mother; in the presence of that Buddha, we both resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Diligently applying skillful means to bring sentient beings to maturity, from that time until the era of Tathāgata Śikhin, and likewise during the time of Tathāgata Viśvabhū, and continuing through this Great Bhadrakalpa up to the first Tathāgata named Krakucchanda.
Since that Buddha appeared in the world, we have constantly acted as brothers born of the same mother through our great vows.
Toward that Tathāgata, we brothers have provided all manner of offerings and supplied whatever was required.
During the time of that Buddha, this man of noble character conceived the thought of becoming an upāsaka; delighting in the cultivation of meditative concentration, he made this vow:
"May I always become a great yakṣa general throughout this Great Bhadrakalpa."

If there are yakṣas dwelling in desolate wildernesses who constantly harbor malicious intentions toward sentient beings and lack compassion—whether they take the forms of various kinds of yakṣas or even kaṭapūtanas—I shall employ skillful means to manifest in a form identical to theirs, preach the True Dharma to them so that they may give rise to pure faith, and once they have attained pure faith, cause them to receive the precepts and establish them upon the auspicious, peaceful, and virtuous path.
Furthermore, in whatever places there may be, among the various realms of animals—such as deer, wild boar, tigers, wolves, pigs, sheep, dogs, and so forth—he likewise preaches the Dharma for them.
Even for as many evil yakṣas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, he performs the same deeds for all those in the animal realm, preaching the Dharma to cause them to plant roots of goodness.
"Once they have been matured, I shall establish them upon the right path of the three vehicles, and only then shall I receive the prediction of my attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The yakṣa Jñānolkā vowed to take the form of a monkey in order to mature monkeys;
the yakṣa Tṛṣṇātyāga vowed to take the form of a ram in order to mature those beings dwelling in the eight unfavorable conditions (*aṣṭākṣaṇa*).
The yakṣa Dantamukha, who vowed to take the form of an elephant, did so for the sake of bringing elephants and others to spiritual maturity.

Likewise, these twelve thousand great yakṣas of supernormal power who dwell throughout the four continents have, since ancient times, made various vows for the sake of maturing sentient beings and seeking anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. At the time they sought anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the presence of that Tathāgata Krakucchanda, they did so specifically to bring wicked yakṣas to maturity.

"May all those evil yakṣas throughout this Great Bhadrakalpa—those who lack compassion, who delight in performing evil deeds, and who lack a heart of kindness; even down to the kaṭapūtanas who steal vital energy, those who derange the minds of others, those who harbor unwholesome thoughts, those who kill and harm sentient beings, and even those with wrong views;
those who cause the minds of kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and others to go mad;
and those who cause madness within roads, cities, towns, districts, and kingdoms—to be utterly extinguished."

They create various calamities and portents, causing the movements of the stars, the sun, and the moon, as well as the measures of day and night, the half-months, months, seasons, and years, all to fall out of their proper course. They incite strife and scheming, famine and disease, foreign enemies, unseasonable winds and rains, extreme cold and extreme heat; they gather together such evil matters to destroy the seeds, medicinal herbs, flowers, fruits, juices, and flavors.

They seek to cause the extinction and disappearance of the joy and happiness of sentient beings, their freedom from illness, their harmony, their desire for wholesome dharmas, the vitality of the earth, and their wealth, grain, and treasures—extinguishing the flavor of food, the flavor of the Dharma, and the flavor of liberation.

When such evil yakṣas as these have been instructed to receive the precepts and established upon the stage of non-retrogression, only then shall I receive the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

"Since that time, I have been constantly born among the various evil great yakṣas as a great military commander, and even among the most wicked kaṭapūtanas and so forth; through the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, I have brought them to maturity and established them, placing them on the stage of non-retrogression."

From that time forward, whenever I have seen ghosts of inferior, middling, or superior rank, I have never treated them with contempt or deceit. According to their manifested forms, I have assumed corresponding forms and spoken to them in accordance with their kind. I have guided them through gradual progress to inspire joy in them, causing them to sever all evils and establish a mind of compassion. Once their aspirations were fulfilled, I instructed them to make offerings to the Triple Gem—the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha—thereby ensuring they would not regress.
"Wherever there is a gathering of yakṣa followers, I shall go there to instruct them with the Dharma; and wherever those yakṣas dwell, upon seeing me approach, they shall all say together:
'Welcome, Aṭavaka!'"
"Because they call my name 'Aṭavaka,' I am named Aṭavaka.

If people of the present time lack the Dharma of the former sages, abide in evil precepts, and constantly perform dark deeds, they will, after the end of their lives, be reborn in the three evil realms; only a small portion of beings will be reborn among humans."

If one engages in mixed karma, yet occasionally possesses pure faith toward the Triple Gem, then upon the end of that life, due to that mixed karma, they will be reborn among various evil yakṣas and kaṭapūtanas, further increasing their numbers within the world.

All their skillful means pertaining to the side of wholesome qualities (*śukla-dharma*) have been destroyed; because of that evil, strife now increases twofold. Furthermore, I am unable at all times to establish even the wicked yakṣas, up to the wicked pūtanas, in wholesome qualities through gentle speech.

"Furthermore, I am unable at all times to eliminate disturbances among śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, as well as among men and women, the elderly and the young, and boys and girls."
Furthermore, I am unable at all times to eliminate disturbances in cities, towns, prefectures, counties, kingdoms, and along roads.
Nor am I able at all times to cause the minds and mental factors of all ghosts and spirits to dwell in the flavor of liberation.

“Good son! By virtue of the majestic power of all Buddhas, I have now attained the skillful entry into the minds of all yakṣas, kaṭapūtanas, and others, including their expedient means and their deceitful thoughts.”
“Good son! There is a dhāraṇī called the Great Fierce and Malevolent Vidyā-mantra that Strikes the Hearts of All Ghosts, known as Vajrakhaṣarpaṇi.

If there be anyone who practices this mantra, then the yakṣīs, yakṣa fathers and mothers, yakṣa sons and daughters, yakṣa husbands and wives, along with their retinues; the rākṣasas and rākṣasīs; even the nāgas and nāgīs; the kumbhāṇḍas and kumbhāṇḍīs; the spirits of epilepsy and the spirits of malaria—whether those that afflict daily or those that afflict every fourth day; and the kaṭapūtanas, kaṭapūtanīs, kaṭapūtana fathers and mothers, kaṭapūtana sons and daughters, kaṭapūtana husbands and wives, along with their retinues—shall no longer be able to harass or disturb the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, or śūdras, nor even the entire kingdom.
"Furthermore, good son!

In whatever place—whether in cities, prefectures, or counties, or within royal palaces, down to the homes of commoners—one should everywhere reveal this Great Fierce and Evil Vidyā-mantra, the Heart of All Ghosts, known as the Vajrakhaṣarpi."

May all the malevolent yakṣas, kaṭapūtanas, and others dwelling in that place—who have pursued [beings] with hatred and jealousy since time immemorial—abandon their unwholesome karma and give rise to a mind of compassion and gentleness, conceiving thoughts of benefiting all sentient beings.

If all villages and households are disturbed by devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kaṭapūtanas, and the like; if they are afflicted by all manner of calamities and portents from the sun, moon, and stars, or by poisonous vapors; if they are troubled by malevolent spells and sorcery; or if they are afflicted by bodily ailments such as wind-disorders, jaundice, disorders of the reproductive organs, and malaria—whether occurring daily, or every second, third, or fourth day—as well as leprosy, ringworm, scabies, coughs, smallpox, abdominal pains, and diseases of the limbs and joints—all these shall be extinguished.

May humans, non-humans, and even birds and beasts diligently cultivate pure deeds and sever all fears; may they be endowed with joy and happiness, experiencing bliss day and night; may they practice generosity, self-restraint, and the guarding of body and speech without indolence, and diligently cultivate the path of seeking aid to assist in attaining Bodhi.
He further spoke these words:
"O son of good family!

The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, rejoice and grant their empowerment, bestowing upon me this mantra of accomplished action, which can eliminate all disturbing and evil dharmas, sever all unwholesome factors, and increase all wholesome factors."
I now wish to proclaim these mantra syllables of the Great Vidyā of All Evil Vajra-khasarpaṇī; may the Tathāgata Śākyamuni grant his protection so that I may expound them with a perfect voice.

If my perfect voice were to proclaim these written words, its sound filling all Buddha-fields, then this great assembly of those who have come would hear this proclamation of perfect sounds, phrases, meanings, and letters, and all would be made to rejoice.
At that time, the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, addressed Aṭavaka, the Great General of the Yakṣa Army, saying:
"O son of good family!

We Buddhas have already bestowed our protection upon this great, violent, and fierce *dhāraṇī* mantra of the Heart of All Ghosts, the Vajrakhaṣarpi, which you have expounded with this perfect voice; it shall destroy the dark faction and cause the radiant White Dharma to flourish."
"Noble son!

You should be courageous and proclaim this Great Fierce Vidyā-mantra of the Heart of the Vajra Khaṣarppaṇī, which removes all disturbances and haunts spirits, and which cuts off all evil incantations."
At that time, the Great Yakṣa General Aṭavaka rose from his seat, bowed with palms joined toward Śākyamuni Tathāgata, and with a great voice made this known throughout this entire Buddha-field.
He then spoke these mantra-syllables before the Buddha: "Tadyathā:
dumaduma 1, damadama 2..."

31. *Chū jī fǎn qiú pí* (Ādi-kṣaya-pratyāgata-spli);
32. *Shì xǔ pó qiú pí sà páng qié qiú pí* (Dṛṣṭa-svabhāva-śūnyatā-sapārśva-ga-spli).
"Rakkuṅpī 33, sātasa tuṅpī 34, svāhā 35. At that time,
as the yakṣa general Aṭavaka spoke this mantra, immediately and without interval, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and kaṭapūtanas were greatly terrified.

All those dwelling upon the ground and in the air of this buddha-field were struck with trembling and fear; in a single kṣaṇa, all these spirits joined their palms in reverence before the Buddha and spoke these words:
“Namo to all Buddhas!”
Homage, homage to all Buddhas!
O Most Victorious One of Great Compassion, may you take pity on me; O Great General Aṭavaka Yakṣa, please speak the mantra phrases for entering the hearts of all spirits.

Chapter Thirteen: The Buddhas Return to Their Lands In the *Ratnaketu Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Chapter Thirteen: The Buddhas Return to Their Lands. At that time, all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones who had come from the ten directions, each rose from their seats and manifested the signs of returning to their respective lands.

At that time, the great assembly dwelling upon the earth and in the void were all struck with trembling and fear; the entire great earth shook violently, flowers rained down from the sky, and ten billion musical instruments played in the air. Incense and powdered incense fell from the heavens, and a brilliant light shone everywhere throughout this Buddha-field, while the entire assembly joined their palms in reverence.
At that time, Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, asked the Buddha Mahācandanagandha:
“World-Honored One!
By what roots of goodness shall these sentient beings become fully endowed?”

By how many kinds of dharmas do the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, protect sentient beings so that they may, in future ages, obtain this dharma-gate, and shall receive it, uphold it, read it, recite it, and for the sake of others, extensively reveal and explain it, and having transcribed this sutra, place it within their homes?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Great Sandalwood Fragrance, addressed the Brahmā King, saying:
“It is so, Brahmā King!

All Buddhas protect the six-element bodies of sentient beings in order to subdue the factions of Māra, to extinguish strife and turmoil, to bring sentient beings to maturity, to ensure the long endurance of the sublime Dharma, and to purify the unsurpassed path.”

All these Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and great Bodhisattvas protect sentient beings through ten kinds of dharmas; in future ages, those who obtain this Dharma-gate should receive, uphold, read, and recite it, and having transcribed the sutra, place it within their homes.
“What are the ten?

First, all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas earnestly entrust all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, constantly commanding them to protect those who uphold the Dharma, ensuring they do not give rise to unrighteous actions of body, speech, or mind; instructing them in wholesome dharmas; and providing them with abundant clothing and food according to their needs, always keeping them free from illness and at peace, even to the point of sacrificing their own bodies and lives to protect those who uphold the Dharma so that they remain without fault.”

Second, that person attains mindfulness, wisdom, and eloquence; they proceed with skillful means and achieve freedom from fault; they are endowed with a deep patience corresponding to their aspirations and mental awareness, and their mind, wherever it abides, is like space and like the earth.

Third, by means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), they exhort the fourfold assembly and other sentient beings so that they may abide in wholesome dharmas and attain a firm body; through these three matters being pure, they practice the path of bodhi.
Fourth, they attain the Ratnaketu Samādhi; having attained this samādhi, they are skillfully able to observe the gateways of all samādhis.

Fifth, wherever those who uphold the Dharma may pass away, immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, along with assemblies of bhikṣus and assemblies of bodhisattvas, will constantly appear before them to provide care and preach the Dharma.

Sixth, when the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, teach the dharmas of accomplished phrases, meanings, and syllables, they hear them all and immediately attain the joy of non-appropriation regarding all supreme, holy dharmas;

all their karmic obstructions, at the very last moment of their life’s end as they relinquish their lifespan and die, are extinguished in accordance with the Dharma, just like the extinction of an Arhat who has passed away.

Seventh, they are born by transformation according to their wishes within pure Buddha-fields as they have desired; those World-Honored Ones remain in the world to nurture them, constantly preaching the pure teachings of the Mahāyāna;
and those who uphold the Dharma abide with a mind like space, fully endowed with unobstructed wisdom regarding this Mahāyāna.
Eighth, they shall not long remain before fully attaining all these merits.
Ninth, those who uphold the Dharma shall no longer take birth in defiled buddha-fields, except by their own original vows.
Tenth, one shall swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
These are the ten dharmas.

"The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, empower those who uphold the Dharma by means of these ten dharmas, so that in the present or in future ages, this wondrous True Dharma shall blaze forth. If there be anyone who receives and upholds this *dhāraṇī* dharma-gate, or even merely transcribes this sutra and places it within their home, all the Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas shall protect and sustain that person who upholds the Dharma; they shall be completely liberated from all afflictions, and such a person is indeed a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva."
At that time, the World-Honored One, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, addressed Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors:
"O sons of good family!

All these World-Honored Ones, who have gathered here from throughout the ten directions, out of compassion for you all sentient beings; in order to purify the external environment of this world; to bring all sentient beings to maturity; to manifest the conduct of enlightenment; to cause the factions of Māra to retreat; to establish the banner of the Dharma; to display all the deeds of the Buddhas; to ensure that the lineage of the Triple Gem is never severed; to extinguish all illnesses; to ward off all evils; to protect against all fears; to sever all wrong views; to lead others into the path of enlightenment; to fulfill the ten powers of the Tathāgata; and to exhaust all afflictions and karma—they proclaim this rare and most marvelous sign.

This dhāraṇī of profound phrases and meanings, never before existing and never before heard, protects households, cities, towns, and kingdoms, even extending its protection throughout these four continents, as well as gods, nāgas, humans, and non-humans; it protects grains, medicinal herbs, flowers, and fruits, and guards both the Dharma-preacher and those who listen to the Dharma, so that they may attain the dhāraṇī of non-attachment, enter the wisdom that is like space, and through this single method, attain the knowledge of all modes of being.
"Furthermore, son of good family!

By means of this Dharma-gate, all Buddhas rely upon the wisdom that enters great compassion, and through ten kinds of dharmas, they protect every single thing within this Buddha-field so that it may increase and not be destroyed."
"Good son!
All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas universally enjoy this Buddha-field without any vacancy, for they protect and uphold all wholesome dharmas."

Those who are born in any of the Buddha-fields should conceive a sense of reverence and prostrate toward this Buddha-field, regarding it as a reliquary stupa and as the Great Teacher. This is because those born in this Buddha-field are well able to establish all dharmas; because they have eliminated karmic obstructions and the five heinous crimes; and because they have exhausted all unwholesome dharmas and their undesirable fruits without remainder, abiding instead in all wholesome dharmas.
"Good son! This is the work of great beings performed by all Buddhas in this buddha-field. Good son!"

You all should respectfully receive and uphold this Dharma. If there are those, whether householders or renunciants, who receive and uphold this Dharma, as well as those who have faith in it, you should protect such persons, for the sake of their obtaining benefit and peace and happiness.
At that time, the Tathāgata Kusumaketu, extolling the merits of this Dharma-gate, spoke these verses:
"Even if one were to fill all buddha-fields with pure gold and offer it as a gift to all the Tathāgatas,
it would not equal the merit of upholding this sutra, which is of boundless measure."
At that time, the Tathāgata Jewel Canopy (Ratnacchattra) likewise praised the immeasurable merit of this sutra, speaking these verses:
"If one were to take heaps of gold and jewels And offer them to Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
One would not obtain such merit As does that person who upholds this sutra."
At that time, the Tathāgata Sumeruśikhara likewise praised the immeasurable merit of this sutra and spoke these verses:
"A canopy of the most supreme clusters of flowers, Spread out and covering the void,
Universally bestowed upon all Buddhas, As an offering with a heart of pure joy."
"When the final dharma is about to end, there will be many things to fear;
yet the measure of the merit from upholding this sutra is such that even all the Buddhas cannot describe it.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata likewise praised the immeasurable merits of this sutra, speaking these verses:
"If one gives rise to a pure mind before the Muni, lighting oil lamps with wicks as large as Mount Sumeru,
and joyfully maintains this offering throughout immeasurable *koṭis* of great eons."
Furthermore, there are others who delight in merit and seek a body of unobstructed liberation;
when the Dharma is about to perish, those who preach this sutra for the sake of the faithful shall gain merit far superior to theirs.
At that time, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya likewise praised the immeasurable merit of this sutra,
speaking these verses: "If one cultivates the wisdom of patience, Constantly arouses the practice of diligence,
Gathers the conduct of the body through meditative concentration, And possesses vast and great wisdom."
"In the age of strife during the final dharma,
those who uphold this wondrous Dharma-seal will cultivate patience and diligence beyond compare, and their wisdom shall likewise be peerless.
At that time, the Tathāgata Pure Samādhi Valiant Power likewise praised the immeasurable merits of this sutra, speaking these verses:
"To reveal and teach this sutra-dharma, to receive, uphold, and transcribe it,
to bestow it upon others accordingly, and furthermore to constantly read and recite it,
offering incense as an offering, along with flower garlands and fine garments."
"The various merits thus obtained cannot be measured by anyone.

At that time, immeasurable and innumerable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, extolled the merits and benefits of this sutra as being infinite and boundless. Having finished their praise, they addressed Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors:
"O sons of good family!
All of you should receive this Dharma-gate, which exhausts all afflictive obstructions and all karmic obstructions.
In the future final age, if there are sentient beings who merely hear this sutra, their afflictive obstructions and all karmic obstructions will be exhausted.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, all those in the world who had attained faith—sons of good family, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Ratnaketudhāraṇī Sūtra, Scroll Ten.
